stories.Headline: Microsoft uses AI and lead to increase qubit stability in its Majorana 2 chip
stories.Summary:
Microsoft revealed the Majorana 2 chip at its Build conference in early June 2026 as a follow-on to a previous topological quantum chip. The company used its agentic AI research platform, Microsoft Discovery, to source materials, experiment with fabrication, and automate the necessary measurements. This new device allows qubits to keep their state for a mean of roughly 20 seconds, with some individual runs lasting one minute. These stability results are about one thousand times longer than the one to twelve millisecond range measured on the original Majorana 1. The company developed this technology to improve qubit stability and reduce the overhead calculations required for the quantum error correction process.

Engineers replaced the aluminum superconductor layer with lead and modified semiconductor layers to a mix of indium arsenide and indium arsenide antimonide. Each unit is a tetron, consisting of a pair of superconducting nanowires with specific end modes and a physical footprint of 0.01 mm. The device maintains information about whether the number of electrons on those wires is even or odd, which is measured in one microsecond. Lead was used because it provides a larger gap in energy levels, though it requires unique manufacturing techniques because it dissolves in water. These changes allow a single qubit to perform millions of operations before failing, supporting a goal of a million units on one chip.

Microsoft stated that the stability gains and new materials demonstrate that their overall strategy is sound and brings them closer to a system. The company claims the new semiconductor mix improves the energy window and that the design allows for single-shot checks and joint measures. By using the distributed nature of topological states, Microsoft says they can avoid the need for many independent processors linked together. The company also announced that the Microsoft Discovery platform is now available for other research organizations to use for their own work. Because of these results, Microsoft moved its target date for a practical functional quantum computer from 2033 up to the year 2029.

Outside researchers want further evidence that the increased lifespans are caused by Majorana modes and if devices can control entire superpositions of states. Microsoft is currently working on providing this evidence through additional measurements and data to satisfy the requests of these external scientific peers. Meanwhile, South Korean chipmakers Samsung Electronics Co. and SK hynix Inc. are benefiting from the global surge in demand for AI memory chips. Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan credited businesses and workers for South Korea breaking the one trillion dollar export barrier for the first time this year. He pledged continued support to help exporters overcome challenges in financing, logistics, and trade to maintain their current growth in the market.

South Korea became the fourth country to reach the trillion dollar export threshold, following the United States, Germany in 2006, and China in 2007. Semiconductor exports surged 193.1 percent on-year to 396.8 billion dollars from January to October, accounting for 42.7 percent of the country's total exports. The cumulative trade surplus reached 294.9 billion dollars in the first ten months, more than triple the previous annual record set in 2017. Other contributing industries include shipbuilding for liquefied natural gas carriers, defense companies with arms deals, and the export of cosmetics and biohealth products. The country is expected to post more than 3 percent annual growth for 2026, the first such expansion since the year 2021.

South Korea must now manage trade risks, including higher U.S. tariffs under President Donald Trump, intensifying competition from China, and Middle East conflict. Professor Lee Jae-min warned that a growing presence in global markets could expose the nation to greater pressure and trade restrictions from economies. Experts say South Korea needs to develop other export industries and new markets to reduce its heavy reliance on the semiconductor sector. The articles leave open whether Microsoft can successfully prove the existence of Majorana modes or construct and control entire quantum superpositions. They also leave open whether South Korean automakers can overcome stronger competition from Chinese rivals, particularly in the electric vehicle market.

stories.Headline: Draganfly and DOD Solution sign memorandum to integrate AURA AI autonomy into Draganfly drones
stories.Summary:
Draganfly Inc. and DOD Solution jointly announced on November 23, 2026, the signing of a memorandum of understanding to advance integration of DOD Solution's autonomy technology into selected Draganfly unmanned systems. The announcement was made in Kyiv, Ukraine, according to a GlobeNewswire release dated November 23, 2026. Draganfly is a Canadian-headquartered developer of advanced drone solutions, unmanned systems and software. DOD Solution is an Estonian-Ukrainian developer of onboard autonomy technology. The two companies said the collaboration is designed to combine DOD Solution's autonomy expertise and insights from Ukraine with Draganfly's Canadian engineering and systems-integration capabilities.

The collaboration will explore how lessons from Ukraine can inform autonomy integration and testing against Canadian and allied requirements. DOD Solution's AURA AI platform pairs the AURA SBC onboard computer with AURA OS software, designed to support autonomous functions when GPS or communications are degraded or unavailable. AURA AI brings target detection, recognition, tracking and terminal guidance directly onboard, allowing drones to operate when GPS is unavailable, jamming is active and communications are limited. Draganfly has more than 27 years of experience in unmanned systems. Draganfly's stock is listed on NASDAQ under DPRO, on the CSE under DPRO and on the FSE under 3U8.

Cameron Chell, Chief Executive Officer of Draganfly, said Canada has an opportunity to apply lessons from Ukraine to the way unmanned systems are developed, tested and supported. Chell said working with DOD Solution is intended to connect their onboard autonomy technology and operational understanding with Draganfly's engineering capabilities in Canada. He said the focus is on evaluating how autonomy can help systems perform in demanding conditions. He said the aim is building the expertise to integrate and support those capabilities for customers. Roman Hapachylo, Chief Executive Officer of DOD Solution, said working with Draganfly creates an opportunity to connect their autonomy technology and experience in Ukraine with Canadian engineering and integration expertise.

Hapachylo said DOD Solution wants this level of autonomy to become a core capability of next-generation unmanned systems, and called the partnership another step in that direction. For Canada, the potential benefit includes deeper technical expertise in autonomy integration, testing and ongoing support, alongside opportunities to strengthen Canadian unmanned systems capabilities. For DOD Solution, the collaboration offers a potential pathway to integrate its technology across additional platforms and explore Canadian and allied customer requirements with Draganfly. The initiative is consistent with the broader Canada-Ukraine objective of combining Ukrainian innovation with Canadian industrial and technological strengths through research, testing, technology collaboration and licensing. Lessons emerging from Ukraine highlight the importance of testing unmanned systems under realistic operating conditions, adapting as countermeasures evolve and incorporating user feedback into continued development.

DOD Solution works with unmanned platform manufacturers to integrate AI-powered autonomy across a wide range of defence applications. Its flagship product, the AURA AI platform, combines proprietary software and the AURA SBC onboard computer to enable autonomous navigation, perception, target recognition, tracking and terminal guidance in GPS-denied, contested and communication-constrained environments. Draganfly develops and delivers technologies spanning aerial platforms, autonomy, sensing, payload integration and mission-specific solutions for defence, public safety and commercial applications. Draganfly combines engineering, manufacturing, software and systems-integration capabilities to support customers operating in complex and mission-critical environments. Draganfly says it is driven by a mission to provide innovative, reliable solutions that save time, money and lives.

Draganfly's forward-looking statements address the collaboration contemplated by the memorandum of understanding with DOD Solution and the integration of DOD Solution's autonomy technology, including the AURA AI platform, into selected Draganfly unmanned systems. They also address the anticipated capabilities and performance of such technology, including in environments where GPS or communications are degraded or unavailable. The statements cover the testing and evaluation of autonomy capabilities against Canadian and allied requirements and the expected benefits of the collaboration. Draganfly lists risks including the possibility that the memorandum of understanding may not result in definitive agreements on acceptable terms, on a timely basis or at all. Other listed risks include that the contemplated collaboration and integration activities may not proceed, may not be technically feasible or may not achieve their anticipated performance or benefits.

stories.Headline: Microsoft president Brad Smith says most data centers must stay near users despite Trump's overseas tax threat
stories.Summary:
Microsoft president Brad Smith responded on Sunday to a threat from Donald Trump to impose a tremendous tax on American companies building data centers abroad. Trump made this announcement during a White House press conference on Friday after he returned from the APEC summit. The president did not provide a specific tax rate or a timeline for the policy and noted he had not yet informed his staff. He mentioned an unnamed company planning to build in Finland as his only example for the proposal.

The proposed tax would target overseas infrastructure, though Microsoft currently operates more than 600 data centers across 34 different countries. This threat has created uncertainty regarding combined pledges of 67.5 billion dollars for infrastructure in India made in late 2025. Those specific commitments included 35 billion dollars from Amazon, 17.5 billion dollars from Microsoft, and 15 billion dollars from Google over five years. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated he had not discussed the tax with Trump, but noted the president is very concerned about technology transfers offshore.

Brad Smith said that Trump is making an important point regarding the possibility of keeping advanced AI training within the United States. However, Smith argued that most data centers must remain near their users because everyday cloud services cannot support Helsinki from New Jersey. Analysts from Omdia and HostZealot suggested there are ways around such an order due to latency and data residency rules. They noted that a buyer in Frankfurt would not wait for a page to load from Virginia.

The White House has not confirmed if Trump will follow through with the tax, and some believe Congress is unlikely to legislate the policy. This is because Democrats are expected to take control of both houses of Congress in January. An analyst from Omdia warned that attempting to stop American capital from flowing into other countries could lead to negative trade consequences. The situation remains uncertain as companies weigh their international investments against potential new domestic tax penalties.

stories.Headline: Anthropic adds iPhone app integration, memory import and workflow recording to Claude
stories.Summary:
Anthropic's Claude has added a set of features that the company says could encourage users of other AI assistants to try it, according to a TechGig report published on November 23, 2026 and based on Tom's Guide. The report describes five distinct capabilities, including direct integration with Apple's native iOS apps, which lets users manage iPhone Reminders, draft calendar events, and prepare text messages or emails. The assistant also includes a memory import feature that enables users to transfer personal preferences and professional details from competing chatbots, which the report says helps Claude adapt more quickly to individual workflows. The report frames these additions as features that could draw people away from rival assistants. Claude's custom Skills are accessible through its Microsoft 365 add-ins for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook, and users can teach Claude specific formatting or organizational preferences that it then applies across those applications.

For Mac users, Claude features a workflow recording option that allows the AI to capture screen activity, mouse clicks, keyboard input, and voice narration to create reusable Skills for repetitive tasks. Claude also provides design tools that help establish a consistent visual identity, and users can input existing logos, fonts, and color palettes to create an AI-powered design system for various marketing materials. The report lists these capabilities alongside the iPhone integration and the memory import feature as the five distinct capabilities on offer. The articles do not name any individual who is responsible for the features or quote anyone about them, and the only attribution the TechGig report gives is that the features were described according to Tom's Guide. The report does not say when the features were released or announced beyond its own publication date of November 23, 2026.

It also does not state what the features cost or which Claude plans or regions they are available in. No one is quoted making a claim about the features being the first, the largest, the only or the best. The context the articles give is limited to the TechGig report's framing that the features could encourage users of other AI assistants to try Claude, and the report does not say what happens next beyond describing the capabilities themselves. The second article, a 9to5Mac piece by Chance Miller published on November 21, 2026, is about the author's favorite non-AI features in iOS 27 and does not mention Claude, so it adds nothing about this event. The TechGig report gives no timeline for further updates, no details on availability, and no statement from Anthropic about future plans.

stories.Headline: Indian new-age firms deploy AI in core operations as Zetwerk cuts BOM time to 10 minutes
stories.Summary:
Indian new-age firms are moving artificial intelligence from experimentation to deployment in core business functions, TechGig reported on November 23, 2026. Companies including Zetwerk, Lenskart, Eternal, Delhivery, Meesho and PhysicsWallah reported the shift in recent quarterly disclosures. Zetwerk cut the time to generate bills of materials on its tender intelligence platform ZetSpec from three to four days to about 10 minutes. Lenskart expanded remote optometry to 934 stores in India from 303 a year earlier. Meesho increased engineering productivity by 171 per cent between March and September 2026.

Zetwerk deployed Zeus, an agentic AI platform that lets business teams build tools independently, per its Q2 FY27 shareholder letter. Lenskart's Drysh system lets customers complete most of an eye examination under optometrist supervision, and the company said it is being piloted ahead of a wider rollout. Lenskart's AI voice assistant improved customer satisfaction scores on calls by about 30 per cent in a quarter. Delhivery said self-hosted models cut customer support and proof-of-delivery validation costs by over 50 per cent without compromising quality. Meesho cut the time to move a model from testing to live deployment from 17 days to three days.

Zetwerk co-founder and CEO Amrit Acharya told Moneycontrol that AI is now integral to how businesses operate and that Zetwerk aims to deploy it across every part of the organisation. Acharya said AI can reduce order processing from several days to minutes in sales, and that agentic AI lets business teams build tools independently, reducing dependence on engineering teams. Lenskart founder and CEO Peyush Bansal said AI is a powerful way to expand the profit pool, improving reliability significantly at the same cost. Bansal said Lenskart is bringing more technology in-house, including CRM, talent acquisition and HR management systems. Delhivery CEO Sahil Barua said on the September quarter earnings call that AI initiatives are yielding material improvements in service and cost outcomes.

PhysicsWallah co-founder Prateek Maheshwari said on the Q2 FY27 earnings call that AI helps handle student queries and evaluate answer sheets without a corresponding increase in hiring. Eternal founder Deepinder Goyal wrote in his Q2 FY27 shareholder letter that some repeat orders or restocking behaviour might shift to agentic interfaces. Goyal wrote that agentic-style interfaces built within the Zomato and Blinkit apps will be able to cater to these customer needs. Rishabh Katiyar, partner at Info Edge Ventures, said newer-age companies were early adopters because many founders and talent come from engineering backgrounds. Krishna Mehra, AI Partner at Elevation Capital, noted that some early efficiency gains from AI deployments may be competed away as adoption spreads.

PhysicsWallah's AI Guru platform answered 108.8 million queries from 6.09 million students, and its AI support system resolves about 80 per cent of queries without human intervention. PhysicsWallah is also using AI to translate live classes into 12 Indian languages to expand its reach in southern India. Around 65 per cent of Meesho's engineering pods now consist of a single engineer directing AI agents, according to its shareholder letter. Eternal has built Dark, a privacy-focused AI assistant running on its own infrastructure, which it plans to launch globally in 2026. Delhivery has deployed AI across order processing, proof-of-delivery audits, returns inspection and claims.

Katiyar said many newer-age companies started experimenting with AI two to three years ago, and that declining token costs and more accessible open-source models helped several experiments evolve into fully deployed products, primarily for internal operations. Info Edge's listed portfolio includes Eternal, the parent of Zomato and Blinkit, and PB Fintech, which operates Policybazaar and PaisaBazaar. Lenskart said its AI voice assistant handles routine customer calls and escalates more complex queries. Eternal is using AI both to develop new products and to explore how its existing platforms could adapt to changing consumer behaviour. Goyal wrote that the food delivery and quick commerce businesses are protected because they have embedded infrastructure, coordinate fulfilment in real time and own the outcome.

stories.Headline: HD Moore finds AI supply chain leaks sensitive user data through digital tripwires
stories.Summary:
Researchers discovered that the AI supply chain leaks sensitive data during an experiment conducted in late October and between July and October. HD Moore, the chief research officer at security firm Dragos, planted two million digital tripwires within various AI services. These digital canaries were embedded in requests sent through a sprawling network of widely used AI services to test information leakage. The experiment revealed an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive user data like a sieve and showed how that information is exploited. This research was published on November 20 and November 22, 2026, exposing security breaches, prompt theft, and widespread failures to protect data.

The system uses AI routers, such as Vercel and OpenRouter, which act as brokers or gateways to route prompts to inference engines. These routers select models based on criteria like the lowest price or suitability, instead of using providers like OpenAI or Anthropic. Moore used Amazon Web Services access keys, SSH passwords, unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references as his trackable secrets. He seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider to identify every responsible link in the chain. The process involves decrypting prompts at each hop, including routers and hosting providers, where data is often logged and stored.

HD Moore stated that the findings revealed security breaches and prompt theft across the vast chain of widely used AI services. He explained that attackers compromised three separate hosting providers and used stolen AWS keys tens of thousands of times in API calls. Moore noted that some resellers logged prompts and passed them to people who then used the credentials to access resources. He observed that a Chinese AI lab scraped secret URLs from over half of the prompts sent between July and October. Moore said that the most effective way to prevent leakage is to host AI models using expensive on-premises servers.

The research affects AI app end users whose prompts are decrypted and potentially logged by various brokers and hosting providers. Some users who paid US providers to keep data in the United States found their prompts flowing back to China. Attackers who breached providers searched S3 buckets, secrets managers, and parameter stores while adding their own IAM users to maintain access. Some stolen requests were marked with Zero Data Retention or no data collection flags, but these privacy settings failed to stop attackers. The findings indicate that people wanting to keep secrets private in prompts face a daunting task that will not get easier.

The background involves an AI ecosystem where prompts pass through multiple players, including routers and pools of models in different hosting providers. Some resellers lure prompts to their servers by offering low prices and then turning on request logging to steal data. The experiment showed that some providers ignore end-user privacy settings embedded into flags specifying terms like Zero Data Retention. One US hosting provider crawled a secret URL more than two months after it was used in a single inference call. Another provider ran a scraper that returned for URLs days after requests, regardless of which AI router was used.

Moore suggests that users who cannot afford self-hosting should receive service directly from a first-tier provider with one contract and policy. He also advises AI users to pick their own upstream providers instead of accepting default provider or reseller pools. However, he admits that even using a first-tier provider provides no guarantee that data will not leak, only minimizing the chances. The articles leave open how many other providers are compromised and how the industry will address these endemic security failures. It remains unclear if the identified Chinese lab or the compromised US hosting providers have changed their data handling practices.

stories.Headline: US regulators scrutinize Nscale for providing ByteDance access to Nvidia GPUs
stories.Summary:
The US Bureau of Industry and Security is scrutinizing the London based cloud provider Nscale for its compute agreements. This regulatory examination began after a Commerce Department rule took effect on November 19, 2026, to restrict advanced chips. Nscale provided remote access to high performance graphics processing units to a subsidiary of the Chinese conglomerate ByteDance. The company leased these chips to Spring (SG) Pte. Ltd., which is a wholly owned Singaporean unit of ByteDance.

This arrangement allowed a China headquartered entity to access state of the art computational capacity through an offshore model. The rule requires a US license for data centers providing over 12 million units of total processing performance to restricted parties. Nscale leased 2,304 Nvidia B200 Blackwell GPUs at its Glomfjord, Norway site, which is powered by regional hydroelectric generation. The company must obtain this license within a 90 day window ending in mid February 2027 to avoid enforcement. This requirement applies to data centers in countries including Norway and Iceland under the Federal Register publication 91 FR 74970.

The specific hardware is subject to ECCN 3A090 controls and the new Section 744.24 of the Export Administration Regulations. The US Department of Commerce is responsible for this rule, which aims to stop Chinese companies from reaching advanced AI chips. Officials stated the rule addresses remote access to advanced semiconductors to close a loophole used by foreign infrastructure providers. Nscale warned in its November 12 IPO filing that US authorities could interpret existing regulations aggressively to restrict its services. The company has not yet stated whether it will apply for the required license to keep its biggest customer.

There is currently no indication from the government regarding whether such a license would be granted to the firm. Institutional investors and semiconductor analysts have responded with caution, revising Nscale's valuation target from $30 billion down to $16 billion or $19 billion. The rule affects university research teams and high performance computing consortia that rely on distributed cloud environments for large scale simulations. Research offices must now implement screening protocols to verify the parentage of collaborators to avoid federal grant debarment or sanctions.

Banks also reacted to the situation, with reports that some paused a $480 million chip loan tied to ByteDance. The outcome of this case will establish a benchmark for how the US polices international cloud compute hubs. In 2025, the contract with Spring generated about $24 million, which was 73 percent of Nscale's $33 million total annual revenue. For the first half of 2026, this customer accounted for 52 percent of the company's $140.6 million in revenue.

Nscale used a $105 million Macquarie Bank facility to finance the Glomfjord cluster, with Spring's cash flows collateralizing the debt. To reduce this dependence, Nscale signed infrastructure agreements with enterprise AI leaders including Microsoft and the company Anthropic. The company also has statements of work with Microsoft worth up to $43.8 billion through December 2033. Nscale must now decide if it will submit a formal license application before the mid February 2027 deadline.

A 60 day public comment period on the technical thresholds of the rule runs through January 19, 2027. The industry is waiting to see if the government adopts a policy of presumptive denial for all Chinese affiliated entities. It remains open whether verifiable cryptographic isolation and strict screening can enable continued multi tenant operations for these cloud providers. The articles leave it unclear if Nscale will successfully dilute its revenue dependence on Chinese entities before facing potential shortfalls.

stories.Headline: Thinking Machines Lab releases Inkling 2 Mini local AI model
stories.Summary:
Thinking Machines Lab released the Inkling 2 Mini local AI model on November 20, 2026. This new multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model uses a looped transformer architecture to increase its capacity. It features approximately 26 billion physical total parameters and 3 billion active parameters per token. The model accepts both text and image inputs and supports a 1 million-token context size. It is designed specifically for local AI setups and is smaller than Inkling 2 Small.

The model uses 24 physical decoder layers, but 12 middle layers run three times in a loop. This process makes the model act as if it had 48 logical layers. It uses NVFP4 and MXFP8 expert weights in a mixed-precision format and includes a DSpark drafter. The router selects eight of 128 SwiGLU experts for each token at every layer visit. The hidden size is 2,304, and the intermediate width of each expert is 1,152.

Thinking Machines Lab stated that they believe this is a refreshingly new great local model. They noted that the model is at least comparable with Qwen 3.8 27B in vibe tests. The developers mentioned that more validation is needed for the model. They also released a research artifact that allows for a variable number of loop passes. They observed that using one or two passes makes inference faster but may lower quality.

The model leads in 32 out of 48 benchmarks in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5. These benchmarks cover reasoning, knowledge, safety, alignment, vision interpretation, creation, coding, autoresearch, agentic search, and tool use. It outperforms Gemma 4 31B, Muse Glimmer, Qwen3.8-27B, and Nemotron 3.5 Super VL in these categories. It leads in FrontierCode v2.0 and ties with Qwen3.8-27B on Terminal-Bench 4.0. However, it trails Qwen on AutomationBench-AA v1.0.6.

The model uses a looped core where every pass starts from the output of the first six layers. Information moves between these passes through cross-pass messages using learned queries. A gating controller decides how much of the current input to forget and how much message to add. Each six-layer block contains five sliding-window layers and one full-attention layer. The local window for these layers holds up to 1,024 tokens.

The model is available for use in transformers, llama.cpp, MLX, and SGLang. GGUF 4-bit and 8-bit quants are provided for the Llama App on macOS and Windows. Users can set reasoning effort levels from none to max using numeric values from 0.0 to 0.99. SGLang provides day-zero inference support for production deployments on datacenter hardware. The articles do not state if further versions of the Inkling series will be released.

stories.Headline: China uses smuggling and front companies to bypass US export controls on AI chips
stories.Summary:
China used spies and smuggling to acquire super-powered computer chips from the United States. These illicit activities occurred recently to bypass strict American export controls on high-end technology. A woman ran a Singaporean front company to facilitate these illegal chip transfers. She established data centres in Southeast Asia to house the smuggled Taiwan-made hardware. Chinese companies then leased the use of these chips through this complex loophole.

The scheme requires Nvidia chips made by one specific manufacturing facility located in Taiwan. These chips rely on rare machines produced by a single company in the Netherlands. The U.S. government set export controls to limit which countries Nvidia can ship to. However, the Trump administration signed off on selling 900,000 chips to China over six months. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnik was reportedly lax with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang regarding these sales.

Kyle Chan from the Brookings Institution says the U.S. views AI as a winner-take-all race. He explains that some officials believe achieving Artificial General Intelligence provides an existential strategic advantage. Kenton Thibaut of the Atlantic Council says China views AI as a general purpose technology. He states that Chinese policies focus on making AI useful for society and the economy. Thibaut notes that the U.S. focuses on frontier systems while China supplies near frontier technology.

Chinese firms are affected by hardware constraints and focus on doing more with less computing power. They aim to automate factories and speed up drug discovery to benefit their overall economy. U.S. companies like Anthropic fear their models could run out of control and want more regulation. These American firms rely on the chip advantage to push the envelope of AI development. China seeks to integrate these advances holistically rather than focusing only on a singular goal.

The U.S. has more computing power than any other nation due to its chip access. China faces physical constraints that make discussions about runaway AI models largely moot for them. The Chinese government is predisposed to prevent any societal disruptions caused by new technology. They currently rely on a bridge of smuggled tech to maintain their competitive computing power. This strategy allows them to function while they work toward their own manufacturing capabilities.

China wants to eventually create its own version of the super-manufacturers found in Taiwan. They aim to separate themselves from the Western tech stack to achieve total independence. AI Czar David Sacks has explicitly advocated for selling more chips directly to China. The articles leave open whether the U.S. will tighten or loosen these export controls. It remains unclear if China will successfully build its own high-end chip manufacturing industry.

stories.Headline: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposes shared limits on pretraining progress scored by perplexity
stories.Summary:
OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published loss scores for company models on Sunday, November 22, 2026. He proposed that artificial intelligence labs agree to common limits on pretraining progress. These scores come from a private test set that only OpenAI can run. One reported account suggests that Microsoft AI can also run this private test. The proposal aims to cap progress using a metric tracked across different labs.

The plan requires common limits based on perplexity and other measurements for pretraining. It suggests a first limit on a key metric that can be tracked across labs. Pachocki notes GPT-3.5 scored about 0.99 and GPT-4 scored about 0.91 on log-perplexity. He ties groundbreaking math results to a model near 0.76 and expects transformative capabilities between 0.68 and 0.70. The proposal asks for shared evaluation norms, transparency standards, and red-teaming of safety cases.

Jakub Pachocki is responsible for the essay and the proposal regarding scaling limits. He warns that research could accelerate quickly and pretraining advances could arrive by 2027. Pachocki concedes that perplexity can detach from evaluations that measure actionable abilities. He notes his test data is a fixed snapshot of the internal OpenAI codebase. He argues that a goal of transparency lets labs find transferable ways to compare.

Other researchers say that perplexity can mislead model selection, as reported by Veličković and colleagues. Schaeffer and Koyejo argue that bits-per-byte is not fully tokenizer-agnostic in a November 4 paper. The European Commission and California officials are affected by compute thresholds in the AI Act and SB 53. Sam Altman previously backed slowdown proposals and suggested licensing above a capability threshold in 2023. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman reportedly compared MAI-Base-2 against OpenAI models privately.

The articles state that log-perplexity is the average cross-entropy loss on text not used in training. OpenAI research from November 10 links falling perplexity to a problem with chain-of-thought monitoring. Scaling-law literature from Du and colleagues suggests emergent abilities appear below loss thresholds under fixed conditions. Existing rules in the EU and California measure training compute inputs rather than model outcomes. Pachocki has been chief scientist since May 2024 and previously led the development of GPT-4.

Next, labs must find tokenizer-neutral scoring and a shared dataset that is not a private snapshot. The proposal requires an independent auditor or enforcement body, which the essay does not currently name. OpenAI expects further degradation in current alignment auditing methods and more training awareness in models. The articles leave open how a limit written in private units can be verified by outsiders. It remains unclear if labs will publish scores on common data to make the cap checkable.

stories.Headline: Rachel Adams warns universities face a crisis as generative AI becomes global knowledge infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Professor Rachel Adams spoke about a crisis facing universities at an International Association of Universities conference from 3 to 6 November 2026. This event took place at Murdoch University in Perth, Australia, and included leaders from over 60 different countries. Adams argued that generative AI is becoming a global infrastructure for producing and sharing knowledge during these overlapping crises. She warned that universities must face this crisis directly rather than treating the technology as a neutral tool. The session was moderated by Dr Noah W Sobe, who is the chief of higher education at UNESCO.

Adams stated that AI must be governed as public infrastructure and use non-extractive data practices with fair provider agreements. She called for protecting critical social sciences and humanities, supporting locally grounded tools, and ensuring transparency regarding research and university funding. The University of Virginia is implementing AI across its 12 schools and offers more than 100 AI-focused courses annually. President Scott Beardsley is investing in the Fontaine Computing and Innovation Center and the Commonwealth AI Initiative in Virginia. These efforts aim to establish the state as a source of trusted and responsible expertise in artificial intelligence.

Professor Adams, CEO of the Global Centre on AI Governance, said universities are complex political spaces facing five interwoven crises. She explained that these crises involve university purpose, autonomy, knowledge, access, and critical inquiry, often driven by commercial interests. Dr Noah W Sobe suggested that AI could develop human capabilities based on Aristotle's concept of human flourishing. Sobe argued that universities should help people enact capabilities and create the conditions necessary to realize their full potential. He emphasized that human judgment, not predictive pattern matching, must remain the primary driver behind the design of education.

Students, academics, and researchers are using AI as tutors, summarisers, and co-authors, while universities use it for analytics and triage. Marginalised scholars from Africa and indigenous groups are affected because large language models act as filters for plausible answers. President Scott Beardsley stated that UVA will not outsource consequential decisions to machines but will use AI to support judgment. He believes graduates must be technically literate in AI but also capable of questioning and critically interpreting the technology. Beardsley intends to pair new technologies with old methods like Socratic seminars, oral exams, and the blue book.

Adams noted that AI models are owned by a few actors, mostly in America, creating a divide between compute-rich and poor. She found that less than 1 percent of global AI infrastructure investment goes to the entire African continent. Geopolitical tensions are evident as US export controls limit China's access to chips and Cambridge faces research embargoes. Additionally, the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation has prevented African researchers from participating in global genomic research studies. This reliance on a few tech providers creates platform dependence and risks of agenda capture from private interests.

UVA will continue to study AI's effects on democracy, the environment, work, and well-being through the LaCross Institute. The university aims to shape policy and legislation regarding what AI should do and how to achieve those goals. Adams warned that universities might drift into a client status if they rely too heavily on big tech metrics. The articles leave open how the long-term reliance on AI will impact human agency and the process of learning. It remains unclear how universities will balance cost-saving personalisation with the need to maintain independent educational standards.

stories.Headline: KPMG rolls out KCi AI agents to U.S. audit teams and reports up to 3.5 weeks saved on some audits
stories.Summary:
KPMG LLP announced the U.S. rollout of KPMG Clara intelligence, or KCi, on November 17, 2026, from New York. The firm said KCi leads the profession to an AI-enabled, human-assured audit for audit committees, management teams, and KPMG auditors. KCi embeds specialized AI agents directly into auditor workflows rather than operating as a standalone tool. Auditors direct and review agent-orchestrated workflows, with agents automating routine tasks and first-pass documentation. The launch follows successful use in 2026, with KCi rolled out to more than 125 U.S. teams and 500 teams globally.

KPMG is aiming to deploy KCi in all private company audits in 2027 and plans a structured, phased rollout for public company audits. Automated data pipelines analyze 100% of transaction populations in selected audit areas, identifying outliers, trends, and anomalies for targeted auditor investigation. On some engagements, KPMG reports this shortened timelines by up to three and a half weeks and removed the need for clients to manually retrieve volumes of individual support documents. KCi operates within a governed environment grounded in KPMG audit methodology, professional standards, and the firm's Trusted AI framework. The technology foundation combines proprietary KPMG capabilities with enterprise technologies from relationships with Anthropic, Google Cloud, Microsoft, and OpenAI.

Christian Peo, Vice Chair of Audit and Assurance at KPMG U.S., said auditor judgment cannot be automated but technology helps remove barriers between data, analysis, and action. Peo said that when people spend less time assembling information and more time understanding it, they can focus on where the risk is and what needs to be challenged. He described the moment as defining for the profession, as fundamental as the transition from paper to digital workflows. KPMG said auditors retain responsibility for review and final judgment, and traceability lets teams inspect underlying data sources and corroborate findings. The firm said agents can generate and organize material, but responsibility does not transfer to the software.

KPMG is modernizing its audit operating model by strengthening role clarity, moving supervision and review earlier in the audit lifecycle, and creating greater consistency in how data is organized and used. The firm said nearly 1,000 Audit and Assurance interns attended training at its Lakehouse facility earlier this year on critical thinking, professional skepticism, and evaluation of AI-assisted work. KPMG said the approach simplifies the audit experience for client accounting teams by providing greater visibility into requests, milestones, and engagement activities. The announcement does not present the three-and-a-half-week result as an average across all engagements, describing it as a company-reported outcome from selected work. The announcement does not specify which provider powers each individual KCi function.

KPMG Clara is the firm's global smart audit platform, and KCi is built on it. KPMG said it was the first of the Big Four firms to organize itself along the same industry lines as clients. Over the past several years, the firm has built a secure data and technology foundation across KPMG Clara. KPMG said KCi is designed to evolve as technology advances and is the latest milestone in its long-term transformation of the audit experience. The articles state that KPMG has market-leading alliances with many of the world's leading software and services vendors.

KPMG's planned expansion in 2027 will test how consistently the model can operate across engagements while preserving human scrutiny. The articles leave open which provider powers each individual KCi function. The articles do not state how many public company audits the phased rollout will cover or on what timetable. The articles do not give the number of engagements behind the three-and-a-half-week result. The articles do not say what KCi costs or how the 2027 private company deployment will be sequenced.

stories.Headline: QuEra joins Harvard-led DOE project to use AI for quantum error correction
stories.Summary:
QuEra Computing said on November 23, 2026 that it is a collaborating partner in ASQC, a Harvard-led project that received $12 million from the U.S. Department of Energy, according to the company's press release. QuEra said ASQC is one of 12 Phase II awards DOE announced on October 9, 2026 under the Genesis Mission. According to QuEra, the project will use AI to design error correction matched to the scientific problems DOE cares about. QuEra said the goal is bringing useful fault-tolerant quantum computation sooner. QuEra said Harvard announced ASQC's project details on November 20, 2026 in the Harvard Gazette.

According to QuEra, ASQC will train AI models to find the errors that matter most for DOE science problems including quantum simulation, materials science, chemistry and nuclear science. QuEra said the project will use AI to design codes and decoders tailored to those problems and assemble an AI-driven error correction system that can adapt to DOE workloads. QuEra said results will be tested on its neutral-atom systems and on lab systems at Harvard and MIT. QuEra said the principal investigator is Mikhail Lukin, Joshua and Beth Friedman University Professor at Harvard and co-director of the Harvard Quantum Initiative, who is also QuEra's co-founder and Chief Science Officer. QuEra said the team includes Markus Greiner and Susanne Yelin of Harvard, Vladan Vuletić, Soonwon Choi and Harry Zhou of MIT, Eun-Ah Kim of Cornell, researchers from Los Alamos, Lawrence Berkeley and Sandia national laboratories, Nathan Gemelke and Michael Gullans of QuEra, Krysta Svore of NVIDIA and Alek Kemeny of Anthropic.

QuEra said the project builds on earlier work in which published results suppressed errors enough that adding qubits reduced logical errors rather than increasing them. According to QuEra, an April 2026 preprint by Lukin, Yelin and colleagues described a neural-network decoder that reduced error rates by up to 17x compared with existing decoders and ran thousands of times faster. QuEra said recent work with QuEra and Anthropic used large language models to discover state-of-the-art quantum circuits for chemistry, optimization, simulation, numerical computation and number theory. QuEra said that in August 2026 it reported that Anthropic's Claude, working through Anthropic's Model Hardware Standard research preview, developed control software that recovered a drifted laser lock in 695 of 700 trials on a dedicated testbed, typically in seconds rather than the minutes an expert needs. QuEra said that in Harvard's announcement Lukin described the aim as an attempt to establish scientific foundations for useful fault-tolerant quantum computers.

According to QuEra, Andy Ory, CEO of QuEra Computing, said error correction overhead decides how soon fault-tolerant machines can start doing useful work and that designing codes and decoders around the problems scientists need to solve lowers that overhead. QuEra said Ory said this strengthens and has the potential to accelerate the path toward Libra and its successor Gigaquop quantum computer on AWS. QuEra said Nathan Gemelke, co-founder and Chief Technology Strategist, said hardware testing is where a design meets reality and that the team will run AI-designed codes and decoders on its neutral-atom systems with Harvard and MIT colleagues. Quantum Zeitgeist reported that University President Alan M. Garber said Mikhail is a visionary leader who will do an excellent job driving progress and strengthening partnerships to ensure America's competitiveness in this area of vital importance. Quantum Zeitgeist reported that Lukin said this kind of collaborative approach is really needed and that the team wants to make something no one else has been able to make.

According to QuEra, the Genesis Mission was launched in November 2025 and aims to integrate the nation's supercomputers, experimental facilities and AI systems to advance American research. QuEra said the Phase II awards are administered by DOE's Advanced Scientific Computing Research division. QuEra said error correction is what separates today's quantum machines from fault-tolerant ones and that the number of physical qubits and operations it consumes largely sets how soon a machine can do useful work. QuEra said ASQC takes aim at that overhead by tailoring error correction to specific scientific workloads rather than treating every error and every application the same way. Quantum Zeitgeist reported that Lukin said the team can really see the dreams the community has had for the last 40 years, for the first time, in the direct line of sight.

According to QuEra, Libra, its fault-tolerant system, is planned for Amazon Braket, from AWS, in early 2028. QuEra said QuEra Gemini has been deployed on premises since 2025 and QuEra Aquila has been available on Amazon Braket since 2022. Quantum Zeitgeist reported that Lukin said that as the team builds larger and better quantum computers it will start making more and more scientific discoveries. Quantum Zeitgeist reported that Lukin described exploring corners of the universe where you have never been, like a new kind of telescope. Quantum Zeitgeist reported that Garber said the barriers to discovery are falling rapidly as quantum computing and artificial intelligence expand the realm of the possible.

stories.Headline: Gary Gensler warns that the AI boom is a bubble that could lead to a recession
stories.Summary:
Former Securities and Exchange Commission chair Gary Gensler warned that the artificial intelligence boom is a bubble. He spoke about this risk in a CNN interview published on Sunday, November 22, 2026. Gensler believes this economic bubble could lead to a recession before the 2028 presidential election. He noted that Big Tech is spending five times more in 2026 than three years ago. This spending includes estimates of 800 billion dollars in yearly AI infrastructure costs.

The bubble affects companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, which need trillion-plus annual revenues to be profitable. These firms face competition from Chinese companies like Tencent, which offers the Hunyuan Hy4 lineup. Chinese models cost between 0.07 and 2.00 dollars per million input tokens. In contrast, frontier models from U.S. firms cost between 2.00 and 8.00 dollars for input. Output costs for U.S. models range from 10.00 to 40.00 dollars per million tokens.

Gary Gensler is responsible for the warning and claims the AI boom could end in a bust. He compared the potential collapse to the scale of the dot-com bust from the past. Dean Baker also analyzed the situation, stating that the recent plunge in stock prices is a good beginning. Baker argues that the demand for expensive frontier AI is likely to be very limited. He believes the underlying economics make the current valuations of these AI companies impossible.

Many users are affected because they can access high-quality AI for roughly one percent of frontier prices. For example, the Alibaba Qwen 3.8 Flash model can write 75 twenty-page papers for 47 cents. OpenAI and Anthropic offer low-cost models like GPT6 Luna and Claude Hailku 5.5 for 50 cents. However, selling AI at 50 cents per million output tokens will not generate hundreds of billions. Baker notes that reaching 500 billion dollars in revenue would require an implausible amount of capacity.

The background involves a sharp slowdown in revenue growth for AI companies since the second quarter. These firms must maintain huge double-digit growth to meet their computer leasing commitments through the decade. Open-weight models from China allow companies to download AI and adjust weights on their own systems. This approach protects sensitive personal information and data from being accessed by other outside parties. The market is currently segmented into flagship reasoning tiers and fast, high-volume lightweight flash tiers.

The articles leave open whether OpenAI and Anthropic can find enough users for their expensive frontier models. It remains unclear if these companies can meet their long-term leasing commitments without massive revenue growth. The timeline for a potential recession before the 2028 election is a prediction rather than a certainty. Investors must decide if the current stock plunge is the start of a larger market correction. The long-term viability of the U.S. AI business model against cheap Chinese competition is not settled.

stories.Headline: Anthropic goes public as protesters gather at company headquarters and Nasdaq
stories.Summary:
Anthropic held its initial public offering on Thursday morning, becoming the first company purely focused on artificial intelligence to go public. Executives and co-founders rang the ceremonial bell at the Nasdaq stock exchange to open trading for the company. Protesters gathered in Times Square and outside the San Francisco headquarters to chant against the acceleration of advanced AI. Some activists called for state regulation, and a handful of protesters were arrested in both of those cities. The company is now worth 2 trillion dollars, judging by its stock price after the first day.

The IPO priced 980 million shares at 83 dollars each, valuing the firm at 1.5 trillion dollars initially. This offering raised 81 billion dollars, surpassing the 75 billion dollars raised by SpaceX in June of 2026. Anthropic uses the ticker symbol ANT and is based in San Francisco, while Bybit offers ANTUSDT perpetual contracts. Bybit Stocks debuted on October 12, 2026, and now allows users to trade ANT shares settled in USDC. The World Series of Trading 2026 runs until 10:00 UTC on December 2, 2026, with 10 million USDT prizes.

CEO Dario Amodei stated that Anthropic remains committed to keeping the technology under human control and resisting political pressure. He believes that making right safety choices while building a successful company will inspire others in a race to the top. Amodei and six co-founders each made about 280 million dollars selling shares during this week's initial public offering. These individuals each hold a stake in the company worth about 23 billion dollars at Thursday's closing price. The company is a financial supporter of NPR, which reported on the events of the trading day.

Critics and AI safety researchers expressed worries about the influence of the company and the potential for an AI bubble. Some people fear that AI could go rogue, while others worry about job losses and the impact of data centers. Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co said the pricing shows strong investor demand after a difficult time for Nvidia. Many employees are now millionaires because they can sell vested stock, but some critics believe the company will fail. Residents in Australia are also resisting plans for a new Anthropic data center in their local area.

Anthropic was founded five years ago in 2021 by a breakaway group of OpenAI employees worried about safety. The company has already taken on 6.2 billion dollars in debt and remains unprofitable under standard accounting rules. It has signed deals requiring 900 billion dollars for infrastructure, including 70 billion dollars in the next 12 months. The industry faces a backlash against data centers, and Democratic governors in Texas and Georgia vow to stop construction. This follows the downfall of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

The company must now navigate a potential regulatory crackdown by a Democratic-led Congress when it begins its next session. Dario Amodei previously warned in September that AI could release agents capable of taking over the internet within months. Bybit has added 50,000 USDT in airdrops for users who meet specific ANT trading volume targets by December. The articles leave open whether the company can find a clear path to profitability despite its massive spending plans. It remains unclear if the company will slow development to allow safety measures to catch up with the technology.

stories.Headline: Singapore and Future of Finance Institute launch AI initiatives for financial services
stories.Summary:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Future of Finance Institute launched several AI initiatives for financial services in November 2026. These programs were unveiled during the Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 to accelerate the adoption of artificial intelligence across the sector. The initiatives focus on improving business financing, preventing fraud, and ensuring the safe use of autonomous AI agents. They support the National AI Missions for financial services by providing data and enabling controlled testing of AI transactions. These efforts follow national AI priorities outlined by Deputy Prime Minister and MAS Chairman Gan Kim Yong.

The AI Innovation Arena provides synthetic datasets to developers and research institutions to build solutions for financial crime and scam detection. MAS will provide a synthetic dataset reflecting interbank transaction patterns and scam activities pooled from five participating banks. The Agentic Money Sandbox allows financial institutions to experiment with AI agents that initiate transactions using digital money under predefined limits. FFI will work with A*STAR’s Institute of Advanced Intelligence and Computing to advance locally developed speech-to-text technology into live pilots. MAS will begin a design study in early 2027 for an industry-wide Scam Detection Utility focusing on domestic accounts.

Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong stated that the programs bring banks, researchers, and public agencies together to develop shared AI capabilities. He explained that scam proceeds move through institutions quickly, making it difficult for any single lender to recognize the full sequence. Gan noted that AI could help lenders assess a wider set of indicators to speed up decisions for small businesses. He stressed that greater autonomy for AI agents would not remove responsibility from the organisations that authorize those agents. The Future of Finance Institute will coordinate work to develop common standards and resources for managing various AI risks.

Technology companies are invited to develop lending tools using synthetic data to help start-ups that lack extensive financial histories or assets. Participating businesses will be consulted to see if the proposed AI tools effectively address their specific financing and borrowing difficulties. Financial institutions including DBS, OCBC, Standard Chartered, and UOB are named as the launch partners for the new institute. The initiatives affect developers and technology companies who can now use pooled data to train and evaluate machine learning models. The government intends to explore if AI can help lenders proactively identify businesses that are approaching a financing need.

The initiatives form part of a wider national AI programme that was announced in the Singapore 2026 Budget. The synthetic dataset for scam detection was developed with the Government Technology Agency of Singapore to improve machine learning models. FFI will partner with AI Singapore to develop financial sector talent through apprenticeship programmes and a wider industry network. The government is currently engaging American officials regarding the implications of new United States export controls on advanced computing equipment. These efforts reflect a move beyond experimentation toward the practical deployment of AI while addressing security and governance requirements.

Authorities will assess promising applications against international practices before considering broader deployment as the work moves into the trial phase. The government will not assume that successful demonstrations automatically translate into reliable commercial systems for the wider financial services industry. Future cooperation may expand to cross-border scam detection after the initial focus on domestic accounts and information is completed. The articles leave open whether the proposed AI lending assessments will successfully lower borrowing costs for small and medium enterprises. It remains unclear how the government will resolve the uncertainty regarding access to advanced computing equipment under US export controls.

stories.Headline: Ken Ono urges human judgment as AI proofs raise credit and attribution questions
stories.Summary:
On 20 November, Levent Alpöge announced he used Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis, a prime number problem that was 167 years old. In September, OpenAI proved the Navier-Stokes equations blow up, but experts felt the solution used an unrealistic force as a loophole. On 20 November 2026, Alpöge and Tristan Buckmaster claimed to solve the real Navier-Stokes problem using artificial intelligence to close that loophole. Ken Ono led the number theory team for Epoch AI's FrontierMath project in May 2025 to test large language models. He watched an unreleased ChatGPT model compute all moments of Tamagawa numbers of elliptic curves using work by Manjul Bhargava and Roger Heath-Brown.

The Riemann hypothesis proof was certified by the Lean and Mathlib communities, while the Navier-Stokes problem dates back to the early to mid-19th century. Axiom Math uses Lean, a language where a small checking program verifies each step, to formalize, verify, and extend various mathematical proofs. Ken Ono, a former American Mathematical Society vice-president, is currently on leave from the University of Virginia to work at Axiom Math. The team produced 43.1 million lines of Lean code to formalize the classification of finite simple groups, which was announced in 1983. This classification required decades of work by many mathematicians, and a major gap in the proof was finally filled in 2004.

Ken Ono said human judgment remains essential because mathematicians must check that a formal statement says exactly what the researchers intended. He stated that hope is not a plan and nostalgia is not mentoring while speaking at a National Academies meeting. Ono believes that access to a powerful system is no substitute for what a young mathematician understands, originates, or makes possible. He noted that his father, a number theorist who died in January, compared AI discoveries to the unexpected formulas of Srinivasa Ramanujan. Ono believes that the mathematics belongs to the generations who developed it, even when AI helps to formalize the existing proofs.

Students at a Berkeley colloquium asked about credit, transparency, and hiring two days after OpenAI announced its solution to the Navier-Stokes problem. Terry Tao and other Fields Medalists signed a declaration called A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics to warn about rushed announcements. This declaration also warns about inadequate attribution and the loss of mathematical understanding, concerns that Ken Ono says he shares with them. Tristan Buckmaster, a New York University professor, suspected OpenAI stole his user data to scoop his progress on the Navier-Stokes problem. Buckmaster and Alpöge released an unpolished proof on Mastodon at 8:37 A.M. EST to avoid being scooped by other researchers again.

Ken Ono earned his PhD in 1993 and has since advised 35 PhD students, 17 postdocs, and hundreds of undergraduate students. He has a personal interest in proving that half of the partition numbers are even or that Ramanujan's tau function never vanishes. His father taught him as a boy about Ramanujan, who believed a Hindu goddess gave him mathematical formulas in his dreams. The Navier-Stokes equations model how fluids swirl and eddy, and the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a one million dollar prize for them. OpenAI denied allegations of foul play regarding the Navier-Stokes proof, and reports suggest they took a different route than Buckmaster.

Universities, funding agencies, journals, and employers must now decide what they support and reward as AI continues to solve centuries-old mathematical problems. Ken Ono will argue that students and mathematicians who choose to work without AI should have a voice in these decisions. He intends to ask his students what they originated and ensure readers know who contributed ideas in the work he publishes. Buckmaster and Alpöge have not yet released the certificate for their latest result, though they claimed it would be released soon. The articles leave open how the mathematical community will handle attribution and whether young mathematicians can still find rewarding careers.

stories.Headline: Columbia and CertiK researchers introduce TensorLean to formally verify GPU kernels and find 38 bugs
stories.Summary:
Researchers from Columbia University and CertiK introduced TensorLean in November 2026 to formally verify GPU kernels. This framework uses the Lean language to prove that compiled kernels match a tensor level math specification. The team tested 149 kernel instances, including every kernel from DeepGEMM and FlashAttention versions 2, 3, and 4. They proved 83 instances correct and found 38 correctness bugs in the remaining 66 kernels. One discovered FlashAttention 4 data race had never appeared during 17,760 separate test runs.

The system requires a 1.8K line PTX parser and runs on a 16 core workstation. It checks PTX compiled for B200, H100, and A100 kernels using Z3 and cvc5. Specifications total 10,278 lines against 151,285 lines of source, creating a ratio near 15 to 1. Developers write five spec parts, including spec math, spec mut, spec layout, spec tol, and requires. TensorLean proves four properties, which are termination, no data races, untouched memory, and correct output within tolerance.

The researchers from Columbia and CertiK are responsible for building this formal verification system. They stated that silent errors in kernels are costlier than chip failures because they affect every GPU. The team noted that equivalence checkers usually unroll loops for one setup, but TensorLean uses symbolic parameters. They explained that race freedom proofs on the happens before graph cover all threads and loop iterations. They also mentioned that developers can add tensorlean assert hints in source code to be reused.

The TensorLean team noted that one percent of wasted compute costs millions at the billion dollar scale. This affects big tech firms like Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta, who plan 725 billion dollars in 2026. FlashAttention users, including models like Grok, Gemma 2, and Mistral 7B, are affected by these kernel bugs. The team reported 38 bugs upstream, including 23 in FlashAttention, 7 in Liger Kernel, and 3 in TileOPs. Other affected projects include Triton with one bug and TileLang and DeepGEMM with two bugs each.

GPU kernels are small programs that tell hardware how to multiply numbers or compute attention for AI models. These kernels are highly valuable but hard to check because bugs often produce wrong numbers without crashing. Training runs for large models have grown 2.4 times a year since 2016 and may pass one billion dollars. Meta's Llama 3 405B run on 16,384 H100 GPUs saw 419 interruptions over 54 days. Google estimated one silent data corruption event every one to two weeks during Gemini training.

The system categorizes bugs into 19 memory access errors, 13 numerical bugs, and 7 data races. It also found 5 undefined behaviors, 5 uninitialized memory reads, 3 algorithm errors, 2 miscompilations, and 1 deadlock. Of 102 FlashAttention instances, 56 passed all properties while 46 failed due to source bugs. Median check time is 10 minutes, with a maximum of 50 minutes per kernel. The articles leave open how this framework will be integrated into standard AI development pipelines.

stories.Headline: US Commerce Department restricts Chinese remote access to super intelligence chips and servers
stories.Summary:
The U.S. Commerce Department announced new restrictions on Monday, November 17, 2026, regarding remote access to super intelligence chips and servers. These rules aim to stop Chinese companies from bypassing sales limits by renting computer time in other countries. The Bureau of Industry and Security issued the interim final rule under the National Security Council and Treasury Department. These measures target cloud services and contract manufacturing at overseas foundries to prevent indirect access to advanced technology. The regulations officially took effect on November 19, 2026, to tighten controls over these alternative computing channels.

Suppliers need government permission for data centers providing power equal to roughly 330 advanced Nvidia chips to restricted entities. Licenses are now required for chip exports to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand due to higher diversion risks. Data centers and exporters must conduct due diligence to identify owners from Macau or Chinese state owned enterprises. Restrictions also cover Cuba, Iran, North Korea, and Russia, while foreign foundries need licenses for Chinese company manufacturing. TSMC and Samsung suspended shipments for nodes 16 nanometers or below, limiting Chinese firms to 28nm and 40nm nodes.

The Commerce Department stated the rule aligns remote access safeguards with existing controls on the physical shipment of sensitive technology. They noted that rapid advances in cloud infrastructure make it easier to access U.S. capabilities remotely through other countries. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Nvidia internal controls, suggesting executives would be dismissed if the company were a bank. President Donald Trump mentioned two different views on the approach, with one side favoring friendliness and another risking confrontation. He stated that both positions were acceptable and that he understood the different perspectives within his own administration.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun accused Washington of interfering in trade and overstretching the concept of national security for its benefit. He warned that China would take necessary measures to safeguard its interests after the U.S. violated previous bilateral understandings. Representative John Moolenaar welcomed the rule, stating it sends a message that America is serious about closing dangerous export loopholes. Affected companies include ByteDance and Baidu subsidiary Kunlunxin, who may lose access to Samsung Electronics semiconductor shipments and services. Nvidia established an Export Control Oversight Committee of independent directors and legal professionals to strengthen its internal company controls.

The House passed the Remote Access Security Act in January to restrict foreign adversaries from using U.S. cloud computing services. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned last week after admitting to an affair with a woman recruited by Chinese intelligence. The Justice Department is investigating if Singapore based Megaspeed transferred billions of dollars in advanced chips to Chinese end users. In February, Applied Materials paid a 252.5 million dollar penalty for illegally exporting equipment to China via South Korea. The Commerce Department had previously requested sales records from Nvidia regarding Megaspeed in May 2025 during its investigation.

President Trump will travel to Manila for a U.S. ASEAN summit and then to Shenzhen for an APEC leaders meeting. He is scheduled to hold talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday while these new trade restrictions are active. Congress is considering a defense bill and Senate measures for semiconductor tracking and congressional review of advanced AI chip licenses. The U.S. is encouraging allies like Japan and the Netherlands to align their export controls with current Washington policies. Articles leave open whether China will retaliate with rare earth export restrictions or if the Senate will pass legislation.

stories.Headline: GraniteShares commits $50.25 million in seed capital to its 2x long and short Anthropic ETFs
stories.Summary:
GraniteShares announced on Nov. 23, 2026 that it had committed $50.25 million in combined seed capital to the GraniteShares 2x Long Anthropic Daily ETF (AIL) and the GraniteShares 2x Short Anthropic Daily ETF (ANS). The announcement came from New York and was issued by GlobeNewswire. The two funds are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 23, 2026. That start follows Anthropic's Nasdaq debut on Nov. 19 under the symbol ANT. GraniteShares described itself as an independent ETF issuer and a market leader in leveraged single-stock ETFs.

AIL seeks daily investment results, before fees and expenses, of 200% of the daily percentage change in the price of Anthropic common stock, and ANS seeks -200%. Each fund resets at the end of each trading day, so each day's objective starts fresh from that day's closing value. Both funds reference Anthropic, PBC Class A common stock (Nasdaq: ANT). The funds seek to give traders amplified long or short daily exposure to Anthropic in a standard brokerage account, without the need for a margin account or options approval. Seed capital is the initial funding used to create a fund's first shares so the fund can list and trade, and it helps a fund open with a base of shares in place.

Will Rhind, Founder and CEO of GraniteShares, said Anthropic's listing had drawn strong interest and that the firm wanted AIL and ANS ready for traders from the very first trade. He said committing $50.25 million in seed capital reflected how seriously the firm takes the launch. He said that bullish or bearish on Anthropic, traders now have a single ticker to act on that view, one day at a time. In the earlier article, Rhind said Anthropic's public listing was an important development for the AI industry and public markets. He said that with AIL and ANS the firm was expanding its single-stock ETF offering to include one of the most closely watched companies in artificial intelligence.

The earlier article said both funds are actively managed and seek their objectives primarily through financial instruments, including swaps and options, and may also invest directly in the underlying stock. It said each fund is designed to achieve its objective for a single trading day only. It said that because of daily rebalancing and compounding, returns over longer periods may differ significantly from the stated daily objectives. The funds join GraniteShares' lineup of leveraged single-stock ETFs, which includes NVDL, AMDL, CONL and MVLL. The disclosure said the funds are not suitable for all investors and that an investor could lose the full principal value of his or her investment within a single day.

Anthropic, founded in 2021, develops Claude, a family of artificial intelligence models used across consumer and enterprise applications. Its Class A common stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT on November 19, 2026. The company priced its IPO at $83 per share, above the $70 to $78 range, and raised $81.3 billion in the base offering, the largest on record. Shares opened at $111.50 and closed the first day 17% higher. Third-quarter 2026 revenue was $16.96 billion, up 47% from the prior quarter.

GraniteShares is headquartered in New York City and creates and manages ETFs across U.S., U.K., German, French, and Italian exchanges. It was founded in 2016 by Will Rhind and managed $12.27 billion in assets as of September 30, 2026. Its products span leveraged single-stock ETFs, YieldBOOST income ETFs, Autocallable ETFs, gold, commodities, and core equity strategies. The funds are distributed by ALPS Distributors, Inc, which the disclosure said is not affiliated with GraniteShares or any of its affiliates. The media contact is GraniteShares, Inc., 250 Broadway, 24th Floor, New York, NY 10007.

The articles said AIL and ANS are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 23, 2026, and the earlier article said they are expected to begin trading on November 23, 2026. The disclosure said there can be no guarantee that an active trading market for ETF shares will develop or be maintained, or that their listing will continue or remain unchanged. It said there can be no assurance that the investment objective of the funds will be achieved. It said none of the funds should be relied upon as a complete investment program. The articles did not say what the funds' fees and expenses would be.

stories.Headline: Anthropic shares fall 6% in premarket trading after record Nasdaq debut
stories.Summary:
Anthropic experienced a stock price decline on November 20, 2026, following its initial public offering. The company listed its shares on the Nasdaq market on November 19, 2026. This stumble occurred after a smooth debut that initially vaulted the lab into the most valuable companies. The listing was widely seen as a proxy for the broader artificial intelligence trade. It failed to revive investor enthusiasm for the sector after a turbulent stretch.

The stock traded at US$88.87, US$91.24, and US$87.28, falling about 9 to 10 percent below its Thursday close. Anthropic had an IPO price of US$83 and raised US$93.5 billion, surpassing the US$85.7 billion SpaceX listing. Its market capitalisation was US$1.2 trillion, with a fully diluted valuation between US$1.6 trillion and US$1.7 trillion. The valuation was about 40 times sales over the past 12 months. Shares closed 13 percent below their opening price on November 19.

Kaush Amin of US Bank Asset Management recommended patience and evaluating the company as it reports public results. He stated that the current valuation assumes years of rapid growth for the company. Tejal Patel of SOC Investment Group said a decline is normal but volatility should raise alarms. Harrison Rolfes of PitchBook claimed the growth plan is largely priced in and the valuation is not cheap. Robert Pavlik of Dakota Wealth said investors are skeptical of the market rather than the company.

Retail investors traded about US$772 million of shares on November 19, the most since Vanda Research began tracking in 2012. David Miller of Catalyst Funds said investors are becoming more selective about what they pay for growth. Nvidia and Meta Platforms fell more than 2 percent, while Amazon and Microsoft dropped more than 1 percent. AMD and Sandisk fell 7 percent, Marvell Technology fell over 8 percent, and Intel lost 3 to 5 percent. Wall Street indexes ended sharply lower on November 19.

The AI boom faced pressure as spending, expected to top US$1 trillion this year, may not generate quick returns. Political hurdles to data center construction and leadership turmoil at Nvidia added to the sector worries. Elon Musk's SpaceX went public in June after the second biggest IPO on record and saw sharp swings. Rob Hackel of RF Lafferty and Co cautioned against buying immediately due to fear of missing out. Berenberg's Carsten Hesse stated the current environment is not good for Anthropic.

Index-tracking funds could account for purchases of up to 30 percent of shares by year-end, according to Intropic. Options trading begins next week and could add to the volatility of the stock. Apple is developing an AI agent to compete with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta Platforms. The market now looks toward a potential OpenAI listing, which the company indicated may happen in 2027. Articles leave open whether the current valuation of 40 times sales can be sustained.
