stories.Headline: PACD: Provenance-Aware Consensus Decoding for Mitigating Cross-Modal Hallucinations in Omnimodal Large Language Models
stories.Summary:
Chang Sun, Yijun Tian, Zhenwei Tang, Yuchen Deng, Yifan Simon Liu, Chenxu Wang and Wei Wang posted a paper on arXiv on 23 November 2026 describing Provenance-Aware Consensus Decoding, a training-free framework for reducing cross-modal hallucinations in omnimodal large language models. The authors say omnimodal models combine audio, video and text for multimodal reasoning but remain vulnerable to cross-modal hallucinations, in which one modality improperly influences predictions about another. They say existing training-free decoding methods try to reduce these errors through modality perturbation or relevance-based weighting. The authors argue that interference from irrelevant modality cues during fusion, and difficulty detecting shared errors, can lead such methods to suppress correct unimodal predictions and let an erroneous consensus persist.

PACD has two complementary paths that depend on whether the branches reach consensus, according to the abstract. In non-consensus cases, a step called Relevance-Guided Candidate Arbitration identifies task-relevant unimodal evidence and selectively arbitrates between predictions using alternative candidates. In consensus cases, a step called Provenance-Based Consensus Recovery uses the outranking principle to evaluate the consistency and strength of layer-wise modality evidence for alternative answers, and it selectively resolves erroneous consensus under confidence constraints. The authors report experiments on four omnimodal large language models and five benchmarks across two tasks. They say PACD achieves up to 27.6% relative improvement over standard decoding across CMM, AVHBench and SVHalluc for cross-modal hallucination mitigation, and an average relative improvement of 7.7% over the best baseline across OmniVideoBench and FutureOmni for general audio-visual reasoning.

The paper is attributed to Chang Sun and six other authors, and the abstract presents the claimed gains as the authors' own experimental results. The authors describe PACD as training-free, meaning it is presented as a decoding framework rather than a method requiring model retraining. The abstract states that the experiments demonstrate what it calls the superiority of PACD, a claim made by the authors rather than an independent finding. The posting gives no information on peer review, and it does not say whether code or models have been released.

The abstract frames PACD as a response to the limits of earlier training-free decoding methods for cross-modal hallucinations in omnimodal models. It says those methods may suppress correct unimodal predictions and allow erroneous consensus to persist because of irrelevant modality cues during fusion and the difficulty of detecting shared errors. The paper reports results on the three hallucination benchmarks and the two general audio-visual reasoning benchmarks named in the abstract. The articles give no further details on what happens next, such as publication at a venue or release of the method.

Articles.Title: PACD: Provenance-Aware Consensus Decoding for Mitigating Cross-Modal Hallucinations in Omnimodal Large Language Models

stories.Headline: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang warns against handing control to AI systems
stories.Summary:
Alexandr Wang, Meta’s Chief AI Officer, posted a warning on November 22, 2026, that society should not hand over control to artificial intelligence systems, an unusual message from an executive whose job is to build them. He tied the warning to AI helping to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a long-standing mathematics problem about prime numbers, and said that milestone shows how fast AI capabilities are moving. When software starts contributing to frontier math, he argued, the “someday” timeline for superintelligence gets noticeably shorter. His core concern is control, and he warned that humans may struggle to keep authority over AI systems that are 1,000 times more capable than people.

Wang’s prescription is not to stop building, and he called for intentional choices in AI development that prioritize empowering humans rather than letting machine intelligence outrun human control. He became Meta’s Chief AI Officer in June 2025, after Meta acquired a 49% stake in his startup, Scale AI, for $14.3 billion. Meta’s capital expenditures on AI reached $72.2 billion in 2025, and the company has planned spending of between $115 billion and $135 billion for 2026. Meta launched Muse, a personal AI agent app, in September 2026, and the launch resulted in nearly a 20% increase in Meta’s stock value.

Wang has not limited himself to posts, and he has restructured teams at Meta Superintelligence Labs to focus on human agency and safety as AI systems become extremely powerful. His concerns echo similar warnings from leaders at OpenAI, and the people building the most advanced systems are increasingly the ones publicly flagging the risks of those systems. For investors, the warning complicates a simple story, because Meta has been rewarded for shipping ambitious AI products, as the Muse-driven stock jump showed, and now its AI chief is publicly drawing a line between AI that empowers people and AI that replaces their judgment. Spending is the other variable to watch, with 2026 capital expenditures planned in the $115 billion to $135 billion range, and Wang’s specific claim that humans may struggle to manage systems 1,000 times more capable than themselves is a hedge, not a certainty.

Articles.Title: Meta’s Chief AI Officer warns society against handing control to AI

stories.Headline: UKRI awards 20 Turing AI fellowships worth over £39m to researchers
stories.Summary:
UK Research and Innovation awarded 20 Turing AI fellowships backed by more than £39 million, EdTech Innovation Hub reported on 23 November 2026. Seventeen researchers will apply AI in fields from economic history to clean energy, the article said. Three others will move to UK universities to advance core AI research. The Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council is delivering the awards through two schemes. The article said the projects are backed by government funding.

The Turing AI Pioneer Interdisciplinary Fellowships give researchers three years to apply AI in their own fields. The five-year Turing AI Global Fellowships bring researchers from overseas to work on how AI systems learn and interpret language and social behavior. The 17 Pioneer Interdisciplinary Fellowships began in October 2026. The three Global Fellowships start in 2027. UKRI is funding researchers to use AI to analyze more than a million handwritten wills, detect rare events in dark matter experiments and study underground conditions for cleaner energy projects.

At the London School of Economics and Political Science, Professor Neil Cummins will use AI to examine handwritten wills for evidence of how people lived and worked over centuries. The University of Oxford’s Professor Jocelyn Monroe will use the search for dark matter to develop AI systems that can identify exceptionally rare events. Dr Roisin Buckley at the University of Glasgow will develop AI tools to help researchers better understand underground and seabed conditions for energy and infrastructure projects. At King’s College London, Dr Thiago Sogo Bezerra will combine AI with new detector technology to improve neutrino measurements, with potential applications in nuclear reactor monitoring and safety. Professor Charlotte Deane, Executive Chair of EPSRC, said the fellowships would give outstanding researchers the freedom and support to push the boundaries of AI itself while also applying it in new ways across a wide range of disciplines.

Professor Jonathan May will move from the University of Southern California to the University of Edinburgh to study how AI interprets intent in language. Professor Denny Wu will move from New York University and the Flatiron Institute to Oxford to develop a mathematical basis for predicting how deep learning behaves at scale. Professor Roi Reichart will move from Technion, Israel Institute of Technology, to the University of Cambridge to study how AI models social interaction and emotion. UKRI says earlier fellows have helped train AI researchers, launch startups and shape policy. The article named the universities of Edinburgh, Oxford and Cambridge as hosts for the global fellows.

The article said the 20 fellowships support AI research and its application across disciplines at UK universities. It said the awards are backed by government funding and delivered by EPSRC through the Pioneer Interdisciplinary and Global schemes. It described the Pioneer fellowships as giving researchers three years to apply AI in their own fields. It described the Global fellowships as five-year awards bringing researchers from overseas. It said the three Global Fellowships start in 2027 and the 17 Pioneer Interdisciplinary Fellowships began in October 2026.

The article did not say what funding individual fellows will receive or how the more than £39 million will be divided. It did not name the remaining fellows beyond the seven researchers it described. It did not give the dates on which the Global Fellows will take up their posts in 2027. It did not say which overseas institutions beyond those named will send fellows. It did not say what happens after the three-year and five-year fellowship periods end.

stories.Headline: Vietnam businesses adopt AI faster but few integrate it into operations
stories.Summary:
Vietnam’s adoption of artificial intelligence is rising among enterprises, but its integration into business operations remains limited because of barriers in workforce skills, data and organisational capacity, experts said, according to a report published by Asia News Network on November 23, 2026. The International Labour Organization said about 11.5 million jobs in Vietnam, equal to 20.8 per cent of total employment, were potentially affected by generative AI in 2024. The Vietnam Private Economic Report 2025, released earlier in the year by the Vietnam Chamber of Commerce and Industry, included a survey on AI adoption in the workplace. Citing that survey, Dr Luong Minh Huan, director of the chamber’s Enterprise Development Institute, said AI adoption among private enterprises remains at an early stage. Of more than 3,500 private enterprises surveyed, 76.2 per cent have no AI use, 12.5 per cent use AI at a low level, 8.8 per cent report moderate use and 2.5 per cent use AI at a high level.

A study titled Unlocking Vietnam’s AI Potential 2026, released in September at Amazon Web Services Cloud and AI Day Hanoi, found that 26 per cent of Vietnamese businesses, or around 245,000 enterprises, had adopted AI, up from 18 per cent in 2025. Among those that had adopted AI, about 61 per cent were still experimenting, 23 per cent had developed comprehensive AI strategies and only 8 per cent had integrated AI into their business processes. The International Labour Organization reported that an AI-enabled vision system recently introduced by Hanoi Industry Trading Investment JSC cut inspection time from 20 seconds to five seconds and raised defect-detection accuracy from 95 per cent to 99 per cent, with 10 workers replaced by three senior high-tech supervisors. An internal AI assistant at VietinBank helped reduce document search time by 95 per cent and the time needed to prepare meeting minutes by 70 per cent, according to a bank report, while Techcombank’s Joule AI assistant helped reduce requests for HR policy support by 28 per cent over three months.

Huan said these cases do not represent the broader business community, and that more enterprises using AI does not necessarily mean AI is integrated into operations. Do Ngoc Ha, an official from the National Statistics Office under the Ministry of Finance, said measurement is important for assessing AI efficiency at work, and that the national AI strategy sets a target for the AI economy to account for 6 per cent of GDP. He said Vietnam currently has no official comprehensive measurement of the overall picture of AI adoption and its impact, and that only a number of small-scale studies have been conducted so far. The National Statistics Office is conducting various surveys and creating opportunities to add questions on AI adoption to existing surveys on labour and businesses, he said.

Ho Thi Kim Ngan, deputy head of the Labour Relations Department at the Vietnam General Confederation of Labour, suggested surveys of workers to capture their opinions and experiences with AI adoption, saying working hours may become longer and work intensity may increase, placing workers under greater stress and pressure. Nguyen Tien Huy, director general of the chamber’s Office for Sustainable Business Development, said AI adoption does not automatically lead to higher productivity, and that technology delivers results only when businesses identify the right problems, redesign workflows, standardise data, adjust management practices and prepare their workforce. ILO Country Director for Vietnam Sinwon Park said the organization believes AI should be adopted in a human-centred way, with productivity gains going together with better jobs, respect for rights at work and opportunities for workers to learn and adapt. She said AI policy cannot be only about technology, and that labour laws, employment policies, occupational safety and health, social protection and international labour standards remain important as workplaces change.

Articles.Title: AI adoption rises in Vietnam, but integration remains limited

stories.Headline: Mark Gurman reports Apple Siri layoffs hit older infrastructure while annual release cycle limits AI response
stories.Summary:
Apple's recent Siri layoffs affected employees working on the assistant's older infrastructure rather than its newer AI systems, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. Gurman reported the layoffs in his latest "Power On" newsletter, published on Sunday, November 22, 2026. The MacRumors article carrying his report was published that day at 12:29 pm PST and written by Hartley Charlton. Gurman said employees have yet to notice a major difference in how Apple operates despite efforts to accelerate development. He added that Apple faces growing competition from AI developers that update their models and services far more frequently than Apple's annual operating system cycle.

Within software engineering chief Craig Federighi's organization, Apple follows an internal release calendar labeled A through G, with engineering work tied to specific software versions and launch windows. Depending on the release, the roadmap and features for a major operating system update are largely determined by late summer or early fall of the preceding year. Gurman argued that this structure leaves Apple with limited flexibility to respond to competitors' breakthroughs during the subsequent development cycle. Siri's multistep control of Apple apps is expected to launch in December, with third-party app support following in 2027. Apple is reportedly developing a more advanced AI agent, but Gurman does not expect it to arrive before late 2027.

Gurman criticized Siri's slow responses, limited third-party integration, and seemingly worsening dictation. He warned that rival agents could become difficult to abandon as they accumulate users' preferences and connected accounts. He said Apple's reputation for privacy and deeper platform access could help it compete. Gurman said employees have yet to notice a major difference in how Apple operates despite efforts to accelerate development and spread significant releases throughout the year. He argued the release calendar structure leaves Apple with limited flexibility to respond to competitors' breakthroughs.

Commenters on the MacRumors article responded to Gurman's report, with one saying agile software development is dead. Another commenter said it is ironic to suggest Apple prioritizes responding at all and argued Apple seems content to cede the AI space completely. A third commenter said the only way around this is to decouple Siri AI from operating system releases, as Google can update its apps without waiting for major versions. Another commenter said Apple already does six or seven significant releases throughout the year and that what Gurman asks for would mean substantially less planning and work on the software. One commenter said Apple's releases are largely tied to hardware launches and that competing would require restructuring teams, governance and ways of working.

Gurman's report appeared in his "Power On" newsletter for Bloomberg. MacRumors' guide lists iOS 27.2 features as including Siri AI improvements, Suggestions in Messages, and an Apple Music rebrand. The article's tags include Bloomberg, Mark Gurman, Siri Guide and Siri AI. The report follows Apple's efforts to accelerate development and spread significant releases throughout the year. Apple follows its internal A through G release calendar within Federighi's organization.

Siri's multistep control of Apple apps is expected to launch in December, with third-party app support following in 2027. Gurman does not expect Apple's more advanced AI agent to arrive before late 2027. The articles leave open which employees were laid off and how many. They leave open when the more advanced AI agent will actually arrive. They leave open whether Apple will change its A through G release calendar.

stories.Headline: Researchers present VIVID, a method that preserves inter-frame motion for video question answering
stories.Summary:
Chengqian Ma, Yuanze Zeng, Hongyu Wang, Mingfeng Lin, YiCheng Xiao, Yu Chen, Pengyu Li, WenHao Wang, Yuexiao Ma, Xiawu Zheng and Fei Chao posted a paper titled VIVID on arXiv on 23 November 2026, describing a method for video question answering under tight frame budgets. The authors say current video multimodal large language models reduce comprehension to static multi-image reasoning by discarding unselected frames and encoding keyframes independently. Spatially, whole-frame pooling dilutes small moving targets into static backgrounds, and temporally, dropping intermediate frames or averaging tokens erases inter-frame motion, confusing direction, speed and order. Their method, VIVID, which stands for Visual Inter-frame Variations and Individual Dynamics, is claimed to move beyond static snapshots like human vision, with keyframes capturing core states while inter-frame Patch Diffs preserve neighboring changes within K_f keyframes. Autonomous Delta-Driven Keyframe Planning selects anchors from a 3 fps pool and feeds surrounding patch differences into Dual-Road Change Memory, forming Dynamic Tokens at zero extra anchor tokens alongside a camera-stabilized Active Motion Region of Interest and chronological Entity State Chains.

The method adds 0.22% trainable parameters to a frozen 27B backbone, according to the abstract. VIVID-Small, trained on 50 examples in about 1.5 GPU hours, beats all eleven baselines in overall accuracy across 8,083 questions and trails only VIVID-Large, which uses 3,600 examples. VIVID-Large leads on MotionBench, Video-MME and TempCompass, the authors say. The paper lists eleven authors, and the abstract presents the accuracy and benchmark results as the authors' own findings. The method is described as adding a small share of trainable parameters to a frozen backbone rather than training the whole model.

The authors frame the approach as preserving localized motion and event order when frame budgets are tight. No independent evaluation of the claims is given in the article. The article gives no information on what happens next, such as code release, peer review or follow-up work. The abstract compares VIVID-Small and VIVID-Large against eleven baselines and reports the benchmarks where each leads. Beyond the arXiv posting and the arXivLabs framework description, the article says nothing further about the project.

Articles.Title: VIVID: Beyond Static Multi-Image Reasoning with Localized Visual Differences and Textual Entity Dynamics in Video MLLMs

stories.Headline: Hancom launches Nomadian AI workforce platform in the US and pursues AWS Marketplace listing
stories.Summary:
South Korea's Hancom has begun commercializing Nomadian, an AI workforce platform in which AI agents carry out corporate tasks, in the US market, the company said on Nov. 23. Hancom held a presentation on its US commercialization strategy for Nomadian at the Crowne Plaza hotel in Seattle on Nov. 16 local time and spent two days discussing cooperation with Amazon Web Services. The event drew Eugene Kawamoto, AWS director of Amazon Bedrock and AI go-to-market, along with partners including VisualFeast, ClickIt and TaskUs, as well as local media. Hancom also hired Bill Fanning as senior vice president and head of US business development for Nomadian, and he will oversee business development at the US subsidiary Hancom is in the process of establishing.

Nomadian is built on Amazon Bedrock, AWS's fully managed generative AI service, and Hancom is pursuing a listing on AWS Marketplace as well as indirect sales through managed service providers. In a 3D virtual office, users can build an organization by deploying Ara, an AI team leader, and 11 AI team members assigned by role and responsibility, and when a task is assigned, Ara divides the work among team members for market and competitor research, marketing content creation and sales proposal writing. Users can check progress and review and edit reports and proposals produced with Hancom's 36 years of accumulated core document technology, and the AI team learns the user's working style over time. Hancom plans to release a beta version in December and a global commercial version next March, targeting 10,000 user companies each month from December through February, up to 30,000 in total, and 10 to 15 local partners by next March.

Fanning pitched the ability to build and run an organization with AI before hiring actual employees as Nomadian's core competitive edge, saying the idea is to hand tasks such as customer response and project planning to an AI team so founders can focus on growing the business. He said what the company is strategically focused on right now is the partnership with AWS, and that based on Hancom's organizational foundation and capabilities he will make sure Nomadian delivers results quickly in the US. Hancom aims to secure partners including the US Small Business Development Center, startup mentoring group SCORE, accelerators and university startup centers, with a goal of 3 to 5 network partners before the beta launches in December. It will select 500 beta companies with the best results as "Nomadian 500," supporting them with prize money and mentoring, and will run advertising in major US cities to recruit beta waitlist members.

Hancom held a separate session with AWS working-level staff and met Mark Relph, AWS director of data and AI partners, on Nov. 17 to discuss commercialization strategy. Once listed on AWS Marketplace, AWS customers will be able to subscribe to Nomadian through their existing accounts, and Hancom is also considering an indirect sales model in which managed service providers bundle Nomadian with their own services. The pricing system is being designed to reflect AI workload while letting customers predict costs, and Hancom plans to refine the pricing based on usage data gathered during the beta and apply it to the commercial service next March. The company cites the rapid growth of solo entrepreneurs and small operators in the US as another reason for the market opportunity, and it expects that as more small businesses use AI, Nomadian's potential customer base will grow with them.

Articles.Title: Hancom Takes AI Employee Platform 'Nomadian' to the US, Seeks AWS Sales Channel Integration

stories.Headline: Researchers present a residual-guided framework that cuts airfoil flow-field prediction errors out of distribution
stories.Summary:
Weishao Tang, Mingcheng Lei and Yufei Zhang posted a paper on arXiv on 23 November 2026 describing a residual-guided sequential inference framework for airfoil flow-field prediction. The work addresses deep-learning surrogate models that perform efficiently within the training distribution but whose accuracy often degrades sharply in out-of-distribution scenarios. The framework is built from three Transformer-based components, which are a Flow Initializer for direct flow prediction, a Residual-based Corrector for high-residual regions and a Shock-based Corrector for shock regions. The authors evaluated the framework on an engineering-oriented out-of-distribution test set built from a CFD-based aerodynamic optimization trajectory. The reported results state that the framework reduces the L1 error, the CL error and the CD error by 30 percent, 59 percent and 41 percent respectively, relative to the usual single-step Geo-to-Flow prediction.

The additional iterative inference cost is given as only 0.25 seconds per sample. The authors say these results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective route for improving out-of-distribution robustness in airfoil surrogate modeling. The paper is listed under the identifier 2611.22629. The three authors are named on the paper as Weishao Tang, Mingcheng Lei and Yufei Zhang, and the abstract presents the framework as a way to correct the unreliable local flow field. The stated aim is to improve out-of-distribution robustness for airfoil flow-field inference through sequential inference guided by residuals.

The abstract does not attribute the work to any institution or funding body beyond the author list. The articles give no further details on the training data, the model sizes or any comparison beyond the single-step baseline named in the abstract. No publication venue, code release or follow-up work is mentioned in the material provided. The abstract frames the approach as a route for improving robustness rather than as a deployed system.

stories.Headline: Jerry James explains how to set up local AI using Unsloth Desktop and home hardware
stories.Summary:
Jerry James wrote a guide on November 22, 2026, about setting up local AI. He used Unsloth Desktop to host models on his own home hardware. This process allows users to create a private ChatGPT replacement on a PC. The setup takes about 10 to 15 minutes excluding download times. It enables a whole household to use the AI over a network.

The system requires a Windows PC with a graphics card and Unsloth Desktop. James used an RTX 5090 with 32GB VRAM to run Qwen3.8-27B with 4-bit quantization. Other options include RTX 5060, 3060, 5070, 5060 Ti, 5070 Ti, 5080, 3090, 4090, or RX 7900 XTX. Models mentioned are Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma 4 12B, Qwen3-14B, gpt-oss-20b, Gemma 4 26B, Qwen3-Coder-30B, Qwen3.6-35B, and Inkling 2 Mini. Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini on November 17, 2026.

Jerry James is responsible for the guide and the specific hardware configuration. He stated that cloud providers act like appliance businesses for routine tasks. He claimed that OpenAI and Anthropic drop model quality in their latest versions. James said he wanted to avoid usage limits for research and coding tasks. He chose Unsloth Desktop because he liked the name and lacked subscriptions.

The author claims that cloud experiences are convenient but have ballooning costs. He notes that privacy concerns make moving to local hardware a good case. Users with different VRAM capacities are affected by which models they can run. Those with 8 to 12GB VRAM can handle smaller 9B to 12B models. People with 32GB VRAM can comfortably run 27B to 35B models.

Quantization shrinks models by compressing weights to fit on consumer graphics cards. This process trades some accuracy for faster speeds and lower memory usage. Mixture of experts models run only a few billion parameters for each token. Unified memory on Macs or specific PCs allows for larger model sizes. Inkling 2 Small is a 594B model requiring a 256GB Mac Studio.

Users can now share their local AI via the LAN access setting. They must set a remote password and share the provided network address. The PC must remain on for other home users to access it. Future guides will cover performance, tunneling, and setting up local agents. The articles leave open how to access the local AI across the internet.

stories.Headline: Developer mjwsolo releases open source Localcode for agentic coding on Mac computers
stories.Summary:
The developer mjwsolo released Localcode on November 22, 2026, to provide agentic coding using local models on Mac computers. This open source tool allows users to install the system with one command and run it within their own projects. The software can read and edit files, run tests, execute shell commands, and search code by structure or content. It also scaffolds and launches applications while remembering specific tasks across multiple messages.

The system requires a Mac with Apple Silicon running macOS 13 or newer and at least 16 GB of unified memory. Users must have Python 3.10 or newer and enough disk space for the software and one of 12 available models. These models, which include options like Gemma 4 and DeepSeek V4 Flash, offer 169 different quantization options and download from Hugging Face. The largest model download reaches 161.9 GB, while the smallest is 4.7 GB.

The creator of Localcode stated that powerful and personal artificial intelligence should work for everyone on any device and anywhere. This philosophy led to the decision to make the inference process local rather than cloud based. The developer claims that Localcode represents a first step toward achieving this goal of accessible local AI. Most operations remain offline, although the network is used for model downloads and specific web tools.

Articles.Title: Localcode, open source agentic coding on your Mac with one command

stories.Headline: Researchers present AdaS-ViT, a spiking vision transformer that cuts inference energy via adaptive routing
stories.Summary:
Zecheng Hao, Zihan Huang, Shenghao Xie, Jiyuan Zhang, Zhaofei Yu and Tiejun Huang posted a paper on arXiv on 23 November 2026 describing AdaS-ViT, a test-time adaptive-routing architecture for spiking vision transformers. The authors say existing spiking vision transformers confine spiking tokens to fixed and uniform firing schemes along the temporal, spatial and channel dimensions, which leaves computational redundancy that adaptive firing mechanisms could suppress. Their paper proposes the Adaptive Efficient Integrate-and-Fire model, called AdaE-IF, which consults the attention score of each spiking token and routes salient regions to fine-grained firing patterns while giving energy-frugal coarse patterns to the remaining regions. Building on AdaE-IF, the authors add Spiking Gated Self-Attention and Spiking Local-Gated Unit, which they say enforce selective spike emission at token and channel granularity.

The paper reports that the authors integrated these mechanisms and modules into AdaS-ViT and trained the architecture with a progressive spatio-temporal curriculum that stabilizes the co-adaptation of firing precision and routing masks. The authors say experiments across benchmarks spanning diverse data scales and modalities show that AdaS-ViT consistently achieves highly competitive performance. On ImageNet-1k, the paper reports, AdaS-ViT consumes only 1.02 to 2.45 millijoules per image and attains an accuracy-per-energy ratio of 32 times to 72 times. The authors describe the model as operating in an economical inference regime and say it pushes the energy-efficiency boundary further.

The paper lists Zecheng Hao, Zihan Huang, Shenghao Xie, Jiyuan Zhang, Zhaofei Yu and Tiejun Huang as its authors, and the abstract presents the design choices and the reported results as the authors' own account of their work. The authors frame the adaptive firing mechanisms as a response to the fixed and uniform firing schemes they attribute to existing spiking vision transformers. The reported ImageNet-1k figures of 1.02 to 2.45 millijoules per image and an accuracy-per-energy ratio of 32 times to 72 times are given in the abstract as the paper's results. The abstract states that the experiments span benchmarks with diverse data scales and modalities and that AdaS-ViT achieves highly competitive performance across them.

The paper is listed under Neural and Evolutionary Computing, with Artificial Intelligence and Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition also given as categories, and it carries the identifier arXiv 2611.23728. The abstract presents AdaS-ViT as a test-time adaptive-routing architecture and does not give a publication venue or a deployment beyond the reported benchmarks. The article gives no information on what happens next with the work, such as code release, further testing or publication elsewhere. The authors' stated aim is an economical inference regime that pushes the energy-efficiency boundary further.

Articles.Title: AdaS-ViT: Test-Time Adaptive Routing for Spiking Vision Transformers with Ultra-High Energy Efficiency

stories.Headline: Researchers introduce HypoLoop to revise AI weight-editing plans using scientific feedback
stories.Summary:
Mengran Li and ten other authors introduced a family of native weight-editing methods called HypoLoop on November 23, 2026. This system connects the choice of which parameters to change and which errors drive corrections to experimental feedback. The researchers developed this approach to address prediction errors that are continually revealed during scientific experiments. It uses a loop of observations and validation records to revise fitting rules and editable locations.

The process requires editing plans produced by numerically adaptive, fixed, or LLM-guided policies to compute weight patches through numerical solvers. Internal validation then selects the predictor for deployment, while the system tests these methods across 22 scientific tasks using Claude and DeepSeek. On the Burgers task, reallocating a matched parameter budget reduced error by 58.80% and 47.72% compared to fixed locations. For the DIODE task, positive-residual weighting lowered absolute relative error by 13.35% during internal cross-validation using 33 editable coordinates. Revising the complete plan across multiple rounds further lowered the final absolute relative error by 10.59% relative to a fixed initial plan.

The authors, including Victor C. M. Leung and Stan Z. Li, are responsible for the development of this framework. They stated that their results from SpaceNet7 and Make3D connect accepted edits to improved spatial predictions. The team argued that these findings demonstrate how experimental evidence can shape the update problem itself. They provided the code for the project to allow others to examine how the system revises weight-editing plans.

Articles.Title: HypoLoop: Revising Weight-Editing Plans from Scientific Feedback

stories.headline_source: HypoLoop: Revising Weight-Editing Plans from Scientific Feedback

stories.Headline: Researchers develop O-IN-Bench to test if omni-modal models understand spoken intentions
stories.Summary:
Zijie Xin and seven other authors published a research paper on November 23, 2026, regarding the ability of omni-modal large language models to understand spoken intentions. The researchers developed a new evaluation tool called O-IN-Bench to determine if these models can recognize when a user is asking for help. This system tests whether a model can provide a correct text response or remain silent when no response is needed after watching a video. The study focuses on how shared scenes between a user and an assistant change the meaning of the same spoken utterance.

The O-IN-Bench framework consists of 1,000 samples in English and Chinese divided into five categories and 16 subcategories. It utilizes contrastive pairs to see if a model changes its response based on different scene conditions. The researchers used O-IN-Engine to verify a sample-specific rubric that judges the language, intent, and content of the responses separately. Among 30 different model configurations, Gemini3.7-Flash achieved the highest overall score of 59.6. This specific model passed 74.4 percent of the intent judgments but only 42.6 percent of the content judgments.

The authors stated that recognizing a request and meeting its requirements are separate abilities that O-IN-Bench can measure. They found that even strong models often keep responding when the speech is a conversation between peers instead of a request. The researchers also noted that the best score drops to 25.9 when a reply must satisfy several people. These findings suggest that current omni-modal models struggle to distinguish between peer conversations and direct requests for assistance. The study highlights a significant gap between a model's ability to identify an intention and its ability to provide the correct content.

Articles.Title: Can Omni-modal LLMs Understand Spoken Intentions?

stories.headline_source: Can Omni-modal LLMs Understand Spoken Intentions?

stories.Headline: AI cheating scandal and top scorer’s death push South Korea to question exam fairness
stories.Summary:
The 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test concluded amid confusion tied to emergency disaster alert tones and the death of Lee Jin-woo, the perfect scorer on this year’s Legal Education Eligibility Test. A scandal over artificial intelligence cheating fuelled turmoil right up to CSAT day. The articles say the episode laid bare the underbelly of a “republic of exams” where grades are treated as the measure of success. They say ranking people by tests is considered the fairest approach there. The government reached for button stickers and bounty rewards as AI technology advanced by the day.

Lee, a student in the School of Dentistry at Seoul National University, gained fame in July by earning perfect scores across all sections of the LEET, in reading comprehension and logical reasoning. With the single title of the first LEET perfect scorer, he went through media interviews and YouTube appearances and became a number one best-selling author. On the 15th, along with the cheating confession by the top passer on the tax accountant exam, suspicions were raised about Lee as well. What followed, the articles say, was doxxing, complaints and the opening of an investigation. Less than five days passed before his death.

On the 19th, the day he was found dead after announcing a plan for public verification, parts of the police search were even broadcast live by some YouTubers. On the 22nd, President Lee Jae Myung emphasised a “fair world” and the “principle of fairness” and pledged strict punishment for cheating and a sweeping review of test administration. The police also announced a policy of continuing their cheating investigation even after the death of Lee, contrary to ordinary procedure. Professor Shin Jae-yong of the Department of Business Administration at Seoul National University wrote on an online community that all of this is an extremely, quintessentially Korean situation. He said the public, the publishing world, YouTubers and the media floated Lee to the very sky and are the quickest to cut ties once facts are revealed.

The civic group Transparent Bag Strap, which has criticised an academic-elitist society, said on the 18th that people should not trust the fairness of exams and should question a society that evaluates people by exams. It said what matters is not strengthening procedural fairness to line students up more precisely but posing questions to a reality in which life opportunities differ excessively according to test results. Sociologist Dr. Oh Chan-ho said the case of Lee can also seem like a sad self-portrait of Korean society that shows how important it is judged to land a big hit on a test. He said higher test scores were until now seen as proof of being smart and logical, but the AI cheating scandal has forced a fundamental question about what meaning this format of exam has. Kim Dong-chun, emeritus professor at Sungkonghoe University, said it is unreasonable to rank people strictly by scores, eliminate the majority to create losers and let winners continue to enjoy vested interests.

The articles give as background that last June, immediately after controversy erupted over fabricated Harvard credentials, Kim Min-ji, author of a book, died. They say that even if fabricating academic records and gaining private benefit by fraud rightfully deserves criticism, the repeated pattern of people embroiled in fake credentials controversies dying under excessive denunciation demands reflection. Some interpret the sweeping impact of the AI cheating issue as stemming from its shaking of the very foundations of the exam system that has long functioned in Korean society as the standard for allocating social status and resources. Anxiety is growing that the assessment regime, sustained by the proposition that exams are fairest, can waver in the face of advances in AI technology. In particular, with controversy erupting on the eve of the CSAT, voices gained force saying that fairness may be damaged.

Long advocated out of concern over potential misuse in illegal filming crimes, calls to restrict the distribution and possession of micro-cameras have gained momentum only after being linked with the fairness discourse ahead of the CSAT. More fundamentally, some argue for reexamining the test-centred evaluation system that this incident has brought to light. The articles leave open how the promised review of test administration will proceed and what the continuing police investigation will establish. They do not say what the review will change or when it will report. They do not say what the investigation will conclude about the suspicions raised on the 15th.

Articles.Title: ‘AI cheating’ that shook even the LEET and the CSAT… Questions left for a wavering republic of exams

stories.Headline: Meta launches Muse AI agent and posts 28% revenue growth
stories.Summary:
Meta rallied 6.55% to close at $653.69, driven by strong Q2 advertising revenue and the introduction of Muse, its new consumer AI agent. TradingKey author Arslan Ali wrote the analysis, dated Sep 10, 2026. Meta opened at $653.69 with a latest completed close nearly matching the chart supplied of $653.47. The stock approached the $658.01 to $659.05 resistance level after a series of higher highs and higher lows. The rally was attributed to the introduction of Muse, Meta's AI agent that can work across email, travel, payments and other applications.

Muse is available as a free product and two service tiers at $20 and $100 per month for heavy use. Meta delayed the product from an earlier planned launch in the hopes of improving safety, and now uses isolated virtual machines combined with system monitoring for some activities. Q2 revenue was $60.80 billion, up 28% year over year, and Family daily active people rose to 3.60 billion. Ad impressions rose 14% and the average cost for each ad rose 12%. Capital expenditures were $31.08 billion in Q2 and operating cash was $31.86 billion, with free cash flow dropping to $784 million.

Management still expects to spend $130 billion to $145 billion on capital expenditures for fiscal year 2026, with total expenses expected in the range of $165 billion to $169 billion. For Q3, management still expects revenue in the range of $61 billion to $64 billion with no formal guidance for a downward adjustment. In Q2, costs and expenses increased 55% to $42.03 billion, largely attributable to legal and severance charges. Operating income fell 8% to $18.78 billion, and operating margin decreased to 31% from 43%. Reuters reported that internal testing uncovered several reliability and security issues, including cases in which the agent exposed or mishandled private information.

Australia has proposed legislation in which social networks with a significant user base must provide users the choice to control their algorithmic feeds, including a choice to view content from accounts they follow. The 1-hour structure is bullish, with higher highs and higher lows, and price trading well above the trend line at around $596.90 and the moving average. The next resistance is likely around $658.01 to $659.05, and if this level is broken price may rise to around $669.59, with $683.99 the next level after that. RSI is around 79, above the 70 overbought level and the signal line around 73. If price falls, support may be found around $638.72, and below this support price may drop to $624.31 and $605.54.

The article gives key levels: last close around $653.69, breakout resistance $658.01 to $659.05, first bullish target $669.59, second target $683.99, first support $638.72, secondary support $624.31, third support $605.54 and fourth support $596.90. The article says the stock rally is interesting for two reasons: strong fundamentals for Meta's advertising and the launch of Muse, which provides a direct consumer AI activity path. The article says this path is potentially very large, but in combination with strong advertising fundamentals, security, reliability and return on the $130 billion to $145 billion 2026 capex plan are of equal concern. The article says a sustained hourly close above $659.05 would confirm that the stock can move past the current resistance zone and justify targeting $669.59 followed by $683.99.

The article says the author remains bullish as long as $638.72 holds but $659.05 in combination with RSI near 79 suggests a slight pullback. The article says the case for the investment is shifting toward the company's ability to spend tens of billions of dollars on new AI related infrastructure to create new profitable products, with Muse the most recent example. The article says Meta positioned its AI offerings differently from other early stage AI companies because it has a large profitable advertisement platform, so AI need not become its own profitable business. The article says Meta can fund many experiments and heavy AI usage.

The article says investors are very concerned that Meta's returns on its core business are diminishing, and with the large capital investments investors want to see returns on data centers, chips and AI models. The article says the margin contraction is worth noting, and that in the next earnings release strong revenue must not be the only metric of concern, with more attention to capex, free cash flow and whether margins can stabilize. The article says a clear break above $659.05 would justify targeting $669.59 and then $683.99. The article says the success of Muse could validate Meta's move away from ad based products and services to something more AI related.

The article says the adoption of Muse will prove to be a strong revenue stream from AI. The article says the trust required to use this AI is much greater than a standard chatbot, and that an AI agent the public can use to make payments or send emails becomes more useful the more autonomous it is, but the reputational cost of mistakes becomes greater and much faster. The article says the AI industry is likely to face more scrutiny, especially regarding safety and accountability, which makes Muse a major real-world consumer AI-agent test. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Dario Amodei suggests immersive video games in a private Slack chat to ease AI job losses
stories.Summary:
The Wall Street Journal published a profile of siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei around November 22, 2026. This report claims that Dario Amodei once suggested using immersive video games to reduce political strife. He allegedly made this suggestion to address joblessness caused by artificial intelligence during his time at OpenAI. The report indicates that this specific remark was made within a private Slack chat.

The reported suggestion involves using immersive video games to help people who lose their jobs because of AI. This remark occurred while Dario Amodei worked at OpenAI before he co-founded Anthropic with Daniela Amodei in 2021. NewsBytes reports that this idea was not an official plan for the company. The original Wall Street Journal article is currently behind a paywall.

The Wall Street Journal is responsible for the report, which was relayed by Techmeme and NewsBytes. NewsBytes stated that the video game idea was not an official plan. No direct response from Dario Amodei or Anthropic was found in the reviewed coverage. The exact phrase used in the Slack chat remains unknown to the public.

Critics on X voiced fears that this suggests a permanent underclass kept busy with games. People who fear AI-driven job losses are affected by the implications of this reported remark. Some defenders claim the Journal pulled a brainstorm out of context. Others argue that people need income and meaning rather than distraction.

Dario Amodei has previously warned that AI could eliminate half of entry-level white-collar jobs within five years. In May 2025, Axios reported his warning that unemployment could reach 10 to 20 percent. He has publicly called for policy responses to a large labor shock. These public warnings contrast with the reported private chat about coping ideas.

The public is waiting for the full text of the Journal article and a formal response. It remains open whether the remark was a serious argument or a thought experiment. The date of the Slack message and the other participants are not known. Future updates may come from Anthropic newsrooms or Amodei's own channels.

Articles.Title: Amodei Video Games for AI Job Losses: What WSJ Said

stories.Headline: Nvidia adds Isaac OS and Agile ONE SN humanoid to its robotics platform
stories.Summary:
Nvidia announced at GTC Berlin a major expansion of its Isaac robotics development platform, adding new simulation frameworks, AI training tools, datasets and a reference humanoid robot intended to speed up work on general-purpose robotic systems. The centerpiece is Agile ONE SN, a humanoid research platform built by Agile Robots that incorporates Nvidia's Isaac GR00T foundation model and its Jetson Thor computing system. The robot stands 1.4 meters tall, weighs 40 kilograms and has 31 degrees of freedom, according to the announcement. Each of its two five-finger hands provides 20 degrees of freedom, tactile sensing and force control for dexterous manipulation. Agile ONE SN is designed for robotics researchers and developers and is scheduled to become available in early 2027.

Nvidia also introduced Isaac OS, an open-source runtime framework meant to connect robot sensors, AI models, control systems and hardware, and said Isaac Lab 3.0 is now generally available with tools for training robot behaviors through reinforcement learning and physics simulation. The additional resources include the SimReady Central Library, which holds more than 2,000 simulation-ready robotics and factory assets, and the Human 1M Dataset, which provides human activity recordings and 3D hand-tracking information for robot training. Nvidia is releasing reference workflows that combine Isaac GR00T, Cosmos world models and reinforcement learning to support synthetic data generation and robotic manipulation. The company describes Isaac as a full-stack open robotics platform giving developers models, data, simulation tools and computing systems.

Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of Nvidia, said general-purpose robotics is advancing at extraordinary speed and that the ChatGPT moment for robotics is fast approaching. He said the company is giving developers the tools to bring physical AI to the world's largest industries. Zhaopeng Chen, founder and CEO of Agile Robots, said the breakthrough for humanoids is usefulness at scale, describing one adaptable machine that learns many skills and works across environments built for people. The announcements reflect growing industry interest in combining foundation models, simulation and physical robot hardware to improve the reliability and adaptability of autonomous systems.

Several European robotics manufacturers are incorporating Nvidia technologies into their development platforms, according to the announcement. ABB Robotics is integrating Omniverse libraries with RobotStudio HyperReality to support virtual commissioning, while Kuka is using Omniverse through its Visual Components FactoryLens software. Sereact is using Isaac GR00T and Cosmos Transfer to develop its Cortex robotic manipulation platform, and Neura Robotics is applying Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab to train its Neuron AI foundation model. In mobile robotics, Toyota Material Handling Europe and SoftServe report that simulation-based development can reduce commissioning time by up to 50 percent, and other companies including Schaeffler, Flexion, Franka Robotics and Universal Robots are contributing to or using the ecosystem.

Articles.Title: Nvidia expands Isaac robotics platform with new humanoid and AI development tools

stories.Headline: Microsoft introduces RDMA over USB4 to link Windows 11 PCs for distributed AI model runs
stories.Summary:
Microsoft revealed a new technology called RDMA over USB4 for Windows on November 22, 2026, to simplify running local AI models across multiple machines. This feature, which is currently in developer preview, allows several Windows 11 computers to link together for low-latency distributed large language model runs. By using this method, machines can move data across local memory without passing through the standard networking stack. This approach removes the need for specialized Ethernet or InfiniBand network adapters that are not typically found in standard PCs.

The system requires each connected computer to have USB4, Thunderbolt 4, or Thunderbolt 5 ports equal to the total number of machines minus one. Users must use USB4 cables for each pair of devices and ensure their applications support the Windows NetworkDirect API. To enable the feature, users must turn on Windows test signing, which requires disabling Secure Boot. Early measurements between two PCs showed that the technology cut round-trip latency for small messages to about 28 to 50 microseconds, which is roughly four times lower than Ethernet over the same link. The system scales at 40 Gbps and 80 Gbps, with the latter providing twice the bandwidth.

Microsoft stated on its blog that this technology is designed to make it easier to combine computers for AI tasks. The company noted that the developer preview currently lacks an auto-retry function for failed connections, meaning the application must handle those errors. In a test using three mini PCs with AMD Ryzen AI Max processors and 128 GB of unified memory, Microsoft ran the Qwen3-235B-A22B model across 40 Gbps ports. This specific setup achieved 18.5 tokens per second with 4-bit quantization.

The company intends to release a Windows Insider Build of this technology in the near future. While daisy-chaining USB4 cables is possible, Microsoft warned that doing so reduces overall performance. AMD reported its own results for decoding and prompt processing, claiming 21.98 tokens per second and 117.98 tokens per second respectively on its own setup. This development aims to provide an affordable way for users to expand their hardware capabilities by linking smaller PCs.

Articles.Title: Microsoft’s RDMA over USB4 will make running local AI models on multiple Windows 11 machines a lot easier - XDA

stories.Headline: AI stock volatility triggers market declines and regulatory interventions in Asia
stories.Summary:
US stock futures attempted a recovery on Monday, November 23, 2026, while Asian markets declined. This volatility followed a severe wipeout of technology and chip stocks linked to the artificial intelligence boom during the previous week. The downturn was triggered by the exit of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a weak debut for the company Anthropic. Investors are now questioning if the massive borrowed funds used for AI data centers will generate sufficient returns.

The Nasdaq experienced a 10 percent drop last week, marking its largest weekly decline since March 2020. Taiwanese shares fell 17 percent for the week, which was their biggest weekly drop since 1990, and the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 10 percent on Friday. On Monday, Nasdaq 100 futures rose nearly 3 percent and S&P 500 futures increased by 2 percent. Meanwhile, South Korea's KOSPI dropped more than 3 percent, and Anthropic closed 8.5 percent lower on its first full trading day.

Various regional authorities are now implementing support measures to stabilize their respective financial markets. Taiwan's financial regulator ordered a tightening of short-selling rules on Saturday, and Chinese stock exchanges eased requirements for margin financing. The South Korean finance ministry stated on Sunday that it would deploy market stabilization funds immediately if the benchmark index continued to fall. These actions follow a period where the benchmark index in South Korea slumped to 10-month lows.

The broader AI trade had previously boosted a wide range of stocks, including electricity generators and cable makers. However, these shares have faced pressure in recent months due to rising interest rates. Market participants are now monitoring whether the current recovery in US futures can offset the selling pressure seen in Japan and Hong Kong. More to follow.

Articles.Title: US futures bounce while Asia markets brace for AI wipeout

stories.Headline: Bill Kinison partners with Uare.AI to revive comic Sam Kinison through artificial intelligence
stories.Summary:
Bill Kinison, the brother and former manager of the comedian Sam Kinison, is partnering with the AI firm Uare.AI to revive the shrieking comic through artificial intelligence, according to a report published by Kotaku on November 22, 2026. Sam Kinison, a Pentecostal preacher turned comic, was part of the 1980s wave of Comedy Store stand-ups and became a pop culture fixture through his signature screaming style. He hosted Saturday Night Live, appeared in Rodney Dangerfield’s Back to School and played Lee Arenberg’s conscience in an episode of Tales from the Crypt. He died at only 38 in 1992 when a drunk driver collided into him with a pickup truck. The venture pairs Bill Kinison with Uare.AI, a firm founded in 2024 that focuses on training its models on specific voices and personalities rather than broader compilations of stolen data.

Talent agency Buchwald says the venture will expand opportunities for Kinison across multiple verticals. In a statement provided to Variety, Bill Kinison said Sam was always on the cutting-edge of comedy and entertainment, and that the genius of Uare.ai’s work and the Buchwald agency’s vision were keeping the promise of his brother’s legacy alive. He added that he could not wait to see what Sam will do. Bill Kinison and Buchwald are the parties responsible for the venture, and the statement paraphrased above is what Bill Kinison said about it.

The Kotaku report notes that the living Kinison was known to pass up on selling his image, snapping a contract with Slim Jim that instead went to Macho Man Randy Savage. It also places the deal in a wider context, noting that while many living celebrities are trying to hedge against this exact scenario, the estates of deceased stars have begun pawning their images. In May, ElevenLabs announced that it would be replicating the uncanny voice and likeness of Stan Lee to say excelsior in audiobooks, and Gene Wilder’s estate is leasing his ghost for a Netflix reality show based around Willy Wonka. The articles do not say what form the Kinison revival will take, when it will launch or what it will cost, and they give no further details on what happens next beyond the partnership and the statements above.

stories.Headline: Investors dump semiconductor stocks amid concerns over an artificial intelligence bubble
stories.Summary:
Investors dumped semiconductor stocks on the New York Stock Exchange over the weekend due to continued vigilance regarding an artificial intelligence bubble. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 10.73 percent, and the Nasdaq Composite returned all of its gains for this year. On November 20, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 48,147.33, which was a decline of 1.93 percent. The S&P 500 fell 3.70 percent to 6910.39, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.28 percent to 22,617.73. The volatility index rose 26.20 percent to close at 35.89, marking the highest level since April 2025.

The S&P 500 fell for seven consecutive trading days, which was the longest decline since February 2020. The Dow Jones and S&P 500 entered a correction phase by falling more than 10 percent from previous highs. Nvidia shares fell 14.01 percent, and Micron shares fell 13.89 percent on the New York Stock Exchange. Three-month futures for electric copper on the London Metal Exchange closed at 12,160 dollars per ton on November 20. This copper price represents a 2.92 percent drop from the previous day and a 13.37 percent fall since November 4.

Seo Sang-young of Mirae Asset Securities said the high corporate value of the AI industry became a burden. He noted that Antropics fell after a public offering and AMD reported short selling in China. He also mentioned a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission accounting survey of Nvidia as a factor. Kim Sung-no of BNK Investment & Securities said the Antropic listing and Nvidia issues caused the sharp decline. He stated that selling other stocks to buy new listings shows that U.S. market liquidity is not as good as before.

Analysts say the domestic stock market will likely start with a sharp decline on Monday, November 23. This potential Black Monday is influenced by the strong selling of foreigners in the Korean market. From November 16 to 20, foreigners sold a net 4.5159 trillion won in the regular and aftermarket. Institutions also sold 454.7 billion won during this same period. Foreigners specifically targeted Samsung Electronics with 1.79 trillion won in net selling and SK Hynix with 94.1 billion won.

The market plunge happened because AI-related market sentiment instability did not subside rather than from new bad news. Hedge sales related to options contributed to the plunge because November option expiration dates overlapped on November 20. Copper prices fell because of concerns that AI data center projects will be delayed after U.S. midterm elections. The "Blue Wave" in the U.S. midterm elections is analyzed as a factor in the copper price decline. Copper is used in power generation, transmission, and use, and is used in large quantities for AI data centers.

Foreign selling is expected to continue in the Korean market for the time being due to deteriorated liquidity. The domestic stock market faces a burden as major indexes and indicators plunge. The articles leave open whether the AI bubble vigilance will lead to further semiconductor stock dumps. It remains unclear if the S&P 500 will continue its decline beyond the seven consecutive days. The future of AI data center projects depends on the results and impact of the U.S. midterm elections.

stories.Headline: Brampton students pitch AI fixes for local businesses at first hackathon
stories.Summary:
The Brampton Venture Zone held its first student hackathon over the weekend of November 21 and 22, 2026, according to CBC News. The event, called the Brampton AI Innovator Hackathon, took place at the Brampton Venture Zone, an incubator run with Toronto Metropolitan University. It was the first stage of a year-long program that will partner post-secondary students with Brampton-based businesses to use artificial intelligence to address day-to-day challenges. About 120 students worked in groups of three to four over the two days on challenges from 13 participating Brampton businesses. The businesses want to adapt to AI but lack the teams or resources to do it, said Dione Almedia, the lead of marketing and partnerships for the Venture Zone.

Students worked with mentors, judges and the businesses that supplied the challenges so they could understand each problem and how to solve it, Almedia said. Bilawal Bhullar, the CEO and founder of Sigma Security Services, one of the participating businesses, asked students to draft solutions to last-minute customer requests, such as a jump in the number of security personnel needed for an event. He said this is a frequent problem in his industry and that it is important for business owners to empower the next generation with opportunities to learn about the real world outside the classroom. About a third of the participating students were selected as finalists. Those finalists will compete to work with the 13 local businesses in the first eight months of 2027 to develop their pitches into solutions.

Tomi Tijani was selected as a finalist alongside his teammates Shayan Khan, Ibrahim Mohamud and Isaiah Ozekhome, and their pitch focused on pharmacology. Tijani said the team wanted to show that the health sector is not something that can be played with and how AI can make it a better place. He said the hackathon gave him a chance to demonstrate his knowledge and skillset and to network with industry professionals. He said his LinkedIn connections rose from about 250 to 373 and that he worked not just with his team but with business professionals and entrepreneurs. The article gives no further details on what happens after the finalists work with the businesses in 2027.

stories.Headline: Hyderabad municipal corporation commissions Osmania University to draft AI traffic management plan for 429 signals
stories.Summary:
The Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation has begun work on an artificial intelligence-powered traffic management system covering 429 traffic signal locations across the Greater Hyderabad, Cyberabad and Malkajgiri municipal corporations, according to The New Indian Express. The corporation has entrusted the Department of Electrical Engineering at the University College of Engineering, Osmania University, with preparing the Detailed Project Report for the project. The GHMC Standing Committee has approved 2.83 crore rupees for the purpose, the newspaper reported on 23 November 2026. The proposed system, called CURE-ITMS, will integrate all 429 signal locations within the CURE limits on a common AI-enabled platform, with plans to extend the network beyond the Outer Ring Road. The system is expected to regulate traffic dynamically based on real-time conditions, improve traffic flow during peak hours and heavy rainfall, facilitate the movement of emergency vehicles and enhance road safety.

It is also aimed at replacing the fragmented approach to traffic signal maintenance and regulation with an integrated, technology-driven network. GHMC officials said that at recent review meetings chaired by Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy and the MAUD Special Chief Secretary, officials were directed to modernise all 429 signalised junctions within CURE limits and extend the network beyond the Outer Ring Road. The directions also included developing an Integrated Traffic Data Platform, identifying accident-prone locations and emergency vehicle routes, and testing AI-based traffic management technologies through pilot projects. The state government has also proposed setting up a dedicated institutional mechanism, Traffic Management and Road Safety, known as TG-TMARS, to oversee traffic management and road safety initiatives. The government has already accorded administrative sanction of 77.31 crore rupees for maintaining existing traffic signals, upgrading and rewiring old ones, and installing and maintaining 50 new traffic signals and 15 Pelican signals.

The latest proposal envisages a broader approach, covering the operation and maintenance of existing signals across CURE limits, installation of additional signals and AI-based road safety measures, including traffic signage and allied infrastructure. Identification and installation of additional signals are planned for December 2026. The Osmania University team has been given four weeks to prepare the DPR, detailing the technological requirements, implementation framework and other aspects of the project. The proposed AI-based traffic regulation and road safety technologies will initially be tested through pilot projects before wider implementation, according to the report.

Other markets and commodities also dropped during this period of volatility.

Oracle reached a 52-week low and issued a denial of insolvency on November 20, 2026. This company claimed it secured all funding needed for its OpenAI contract. Senator Adam Schiff wrote in the Wall Street Journal that there will be no bailout. Hedge funds like Situational Awareness were affected, selling portfolios in July. The crash affects superrich managers, Wall Street bankers, and Silicon Valley monopolists.

The bubble grew as corporations used financial models that did not cover debt service costs. Leverage in the hedge fund sector increased after the Silicon Valley Bank bailout. stories.Headline: Machine learning and pharmacology screen finds five approved drugs targeting endometrial infertility subtypes
stories.Summary:
A computational framework combining machine learning and systems pharmacology has identified five approved medications capable of targeting distinct molecular abnormalities underlying non-timing endometrial infertility, according to findings published in Reproductive Biology and Endocrinology. The work was reported on November 23, 2026, in an article whose authors include Parraga-Leo, Sebastian-Leon, Sanchez-Reyes, Sanz, Vidal, Sanchez-Ribas, Quiñonero, Wells, Pellicer, Sirota and Diaz-Gimeno. The condition is described as an idiopathic form of endometrial failure that impairs reproductive success during assisted reproduction regardless of embryo quality. The findings offer a targeted strategy to address this non-timing endometrial failure, the article states.

Investigators conducted a multicentre prospective study evaluating 192 endometrial biopsies collected during the mid-secretory phase from female patients undergoing in vitro fertilization. The research team applied machine learning algorithms to transcriptomic data and clinical outcomes to categorize tissue specimens into distinct good-prognosis and poor-prognosis endotypes, which were then partitioned into discrete molecular subendotypes based on shared gene expression alterations and reproductive trajectories. The poor-prognosis endotype, comprising 43 patients, showed a pregnancy rate of 26.3 percent compared to 66.0 percent in the good-prognosis cohort, with a statistically significant difference evaluated at p = 1.99 × 10⁻⁵. Live birth rates were likewise depressed among poor-prognosis patients at 40.0 percent compared to 87.1 percent in good-prognosis controls, at p = 0.0013. The poor-prognosis group also experienced elevated biochemical miscarriage rates of 30.3 percent versus 7.2 percent, at p = 0.0372, alongside heightened clinical miscarriage rates of 42.9 percent versus 6.2 percent, at p = 0.0159.

Deeper algorithmic partitioning divided the poor-prognosis cohort into two distinct molecular subendotypes distinguished by different failure modes and underlying cellular pathology. The first subendotype, encompassing 16 patients, was characterized by an increased biochemical miscarriage rate of 66.7 percent compared to 14.3 percent observed in the alternative poor-prognosis group, at p = 0.0022. The second subendotype, comprising 27 patients, was associated with an elevated clinical miscarriage rate of 50.0 percent compared to 0.0 percent in the first group, at p = 0.0001. In addition to impaired decidualization, the biochemical miscarriage subendotype displayed prominent immune dysregulation, identifying local immune pathway disturbances as a primary biological mechanism contributing to early embryonic loss.

To establish therapeutic countermeasures against these identified transcriptomic dysfunctions, the authors deployed systems pharmacology approaches to evaluate approved pharmaceuticals capable of inverting the abnormal molecular signatures. This in silico screening prioritized five approved compounds possessing target profiles aligned with the dysregulated subendotypes: genistein, pioglitazone, alprostadil, flunisolide and tenoxicam. The therapeutic potential of the computationally selected drugs was subsequently validated through functional biological assays in human endometrial stromal cell lines using quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, F-actin cellular staining and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Concurrently, alprostadil, flunisolide and tenoxicam demonstrated clear anti-inflammatory properties by inhibiting well-established biomarkers of endometrial immune response. Although these laboratory observations confirm that repurposed compounds can modulate specific cellular pathways in human endometrial cells, the authors emphasized that formal clinical trials in patient cohorts remain necessary to validate therapeutic efficacy and advance these personalized interventions into routine reproductive medicine.

stories.Headline: Researchers teach a 12,000-pound John Deere loader to balance and spin autonomously
stories.Summary:
Researchers affiliated with ETH Zurich, Blue River Technology, Gravis Robotics and Intel used reinforcement learning and computer simulation to teach a John Deere skid-steer loader to perform autonomous acrobatic manoeuvres. The machine is a 12,000-pound John Deere 332G skid-steer loader, an industrial machine designed primarily for moving materials and performing construction work. The team trained it to lift itself onto two wheels, maintain balance, navigate uneven surfaces and execute controlled spins without assistance. The training relied on reinforcement learning, a machine learning approach in which an artificial agent improves its decisions through rewards and penalties.

They first trained the control system inside a simulated environment before transferring its learned instructions to the physical construction machine. The work changes how such a machine is controlled, because the researchers developed an artificial intelligence system that learned suitable movements through repeated training and feedback instead of relying on conventional programming. The loader can spin while maintaining balance on uneven terrain, and it now balances on two wheels without an operator. The researchers trained the construction machine in simulation before real-world demonstrations, and the machine learned movements normally associated with stunt driving rather than human operators.

The demonstrations showed the machine lifting itself onto two wheels, holding its balance and executing controlled spins on its own. The researchers affiliated with ETH Zurich, Blue River Technology, Gravis Robotics and Intel are responsible for the work, and the articles do not give further statements from them beyond describing the training method and the demonstrations. The articles describe the machine as a John Deere 332G skid-steer loader and say the researchers taught it using reinforcement learning and computer simulation. They report that the control system was trained in a simulated environment first, with the learned instructions then transferred to the physical machine.

The articles do not name individual researchers or quote any of them directly. The context is that the machine is an industrial loader built for moving materials and construction work, and the researchers taught it movements previously associated with highly skilled human operators. The articles say the training happened in simulation before real-world demonstrations, and they describe the resulting abilities as autonomous acrobatic manoeuvres. The articles do not say what happens next, whether the system will be deployed commercially, or when further demonstrations might take place.

stories.Headline: Army works with OpenAI to automate software accreditation for vendors
stories.Summary:
The Army is collaborating with OpenAI to streamline the accreditation process for commercial software vendors seeking to provide products to the military, according to a report by DefenseScoop. The initiative, known as Project Gatekeeper, aims to automate the authority to operate process, which historically takes months to complete. By allowing vendors to submit code to an Army development, security and operations platform for rapid validation, the service intends to lower barriers for industry partners. Acting Army Chief Information Officer Gabe Chiulli stated that the project provides an initial vetting process, granting successful applicants access to secure Army enclaves. The Army plans to integrate artificial intelligence models into this pipeline within the next quarter, starting with a phased approach using OpenAI tools.

This strategy focuses on strategic validation to avoid redundant checks, according to the report. Future phases will likely incorporate additional open source and commercial providers beyond the initial OpenAI tools. To maintain security and privacy, the Army will encourage companies to utilize their own application programming interface keys during the scanning process. This approach ensures that vendors retain control over their vulnerability logs while benefiting from the automated vetting system. Chiulli said the project offers an initial vetting process that gives successful applicants access to secure Army enclaves, and officials are also working to expand access to the platform beyond current Common Access Card holders by integrating Login.gov.

The service intends to lower barriers for industry partners through the rapid validation of submitted code. The phased approach using OpenAI tools is meant to focus on strategic validation and avoid redundant checks. Vendors keep control of their vulnerability logs by using their own application programming interface keys during scanning. More to follow.
